column4: Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE:RSG) Delivered A Better ROE Than Its Industry
column10: [Many investors are still learning about the various metrics that can be useful when analysing a stock. This article is for those who would like to learn about Return On Equity (ROE). We'll use ROE to examine Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE:RSG), by way of a worked example.ROE or return on equity is a useful tool to assess how effectively a company can generate returns on the investment it received from its shareholders. In short, ROE shows the profit each dollar generates with respect to its shareholder investments. See our latest analysis for Republic Services How Is ROE Calculated?Return on equity can be calculated by using the formula:Return on Equity = Net Profit (from continuing operations) ÷ Shareholders' EquitySo, based on the above formula, the ROE for Republic Services is:15% = US$1.5b ÷ US$9.9b (Based on the trailing twelve months to March 2023).The 'return' refers to a company's earnings over the last year. Another way to think of that is that for every $1 worth of equity, the company was able to earn $0.15 in profit.Does Republic Services Have A Good Return On Equity?Arguably the easiest way to assess company's ROE is to compare it with the average in its industry. However, this method is only useful as a rough check, because companies do differ quite a bit within the same industry classification. As is clear from the image below, Republic Services has a better ROE than the average (13%) in the Commercial Services industry.roeThat's clearly a positive. Bear in mind, a high ROE doesn't always mean superior financial performance. A higher proportion of debt in a company's capital structure may also result in a high ROE, where the high debt levels could be a huge risk . To know the 2 risks we have identified for Republic Services visit our risks dashboard for free.How Does Debt Impact ROE?Most companies need money -- from somewhere -- to grow their profits. The cash for investment can come from prior year profits (retained earnings), issuing new shares, or borrowing. In the first and second cases, the ROE will reflect this use of cash for investment in the business. In the latter case, the debt used for growth will improve returns, but won't affect the total equity. Thus the use of debt can improve ROE, albeit along with extra risk in the case of stormy weather, metaphorically speaking.Story continuesRepublic Services' Debt And Its 15% ROERepublic Services does use a high amount of debt to increase returns. It has a debt to equity ratio of 1.21. While its ROE is pretty respectable, the amount of debt the company is carrying currently is not ideal. Investors should think carefully about how a company might perform if it was unable to borrow so easily, because credit markets do change over time.ConclusionReturn on equity is useful for comparing the quality of different businesses. A company that can achieve a high return on equity without debt could be considered a high quality business. All else being equal, a higher ROE is better.But ROE is just one piece of a bigger puzzle, since high quality businesses often trade on high multiples of earnings. The rate at which profits are likely to grow, relative to the expectations of profit growth reflected in the current price, must be considered, too. column4: Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE:RSG) Delivered A Better ROE Than Its Industry
column10: [Many investors are still learning about the various metrics that can be useful when analysing a stock. This article is for those who would like to learn about Return On Equity (ROE). We'll use ROE to examine Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE:RSG), by way of a worked example.ROE or return on equity is a useful tool to assess how effectively a company can generate returns on the investment it received from its shareholders. In short, ROE shows the profit each dollar generates with respect to its shareholder investments. See our latest analysis for Republic Services How Is ROE Calculated?Return on equity can be calculated by using the formula:Return on Equity = Net Profit (from continuing operations) ÷ Shareholders' EquitySo, based on the above formula, the ROE for Republic Services is:15% = US$1.5b ÷ US$9.9b (Based on the trailing twelve months to March 2023).The 'return' refers to a company's earnings over the last year. Another way to think of that is that for every $1 worth of equity, the company was able to earn $0.15 in profit.Does Republic Services Have A Good Return On Equity?Arguably the easiest way to assess company's ROE is to compare it with the average in its industry. However, this method is only useful as a rough check, because companies do differ quite a bit within the same industry classification. As is clear from the image below, Republic Services has a better ROE than the average (13%) in the Commercial Services industry.roeThat's clearly a positive. Bear in mind, a high ROE doesn't always mean superior financial performance. A higher proportion of debt in a company's capital structure may also result in a high ROE, where the high debt levels could be a huge risk . To know the 2 risks we have identified for Republic Services visit our risks dashboard for free.How Does Debt Impact ROE?Most companies need money -- from somewhere -- to grow their profits. The cash for investment can come from prior year profits (retained earnings), issuing new shares, or borrowing. In the first and second cases, the ROE will reflect this use of cash for investment in the business. In the latter case, the debt used for growth will improve returns, but won't affect the total equity. Thus the use of debt can improve ROE, albeit along with extra risk in the case of stormy weather, metaphorically speaking.Story continuesRepublic Services' Debt And Its 15% ROERepublic Services does use a high amount of debt to increase returns. It has a debt to equity ratio of 1.21. While its ROE is pretty respectable, the amount of debt the company is carrying currently is not ideal. Investors should think carefully about how a company might perform if it was unable to borrow so easily, because credit markets do change over time.ConclusionReturn on equity is useful for comparing the quality of different businesses. A company that can achieve a high return on equity without debt could be considered a high quality business. All else being equal, a higher ROE is better.But ROE is just one piece of a bigger puzzle, since high quality businesses often trade on high multiples of earnings. The rate at which profits are likely to grow, relative to the expectations of profit growth reflected in the current price, must be considered, too. column4: Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE:RSG) Delivered A Better ROE Than Its Industry
column10: [Many investors are still learning about the various metrics that can be useful when analysing a stock. This article is for those who would like to learn about Return On Equity (ROE). We'll use ROE to examine Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE:RSG), by way of a worked example.ROE or return on equity is a useful tool to assess how effectively a company can generate returns on the investment it received from its shareholders. In short, ROE shows the profit each dollar generates with respect to its shareholder investments. See our latest analysis for Republic Services How Is ROE Calculated?Return on equity can be calculated by using the formula:Return on Equity = Net Profit (from continuing operations) ÷ Shareholders' EquitySo, based on the above formula, the ROE for Republic Services is:15% = US$1.5b ÷ US$9.9b (Based on the trailing twelve months to March 2023).The 'return' refers to a company's earnings over the last year. Another way to think of that is that for every $1 worth of equity, the company was able to earn $0.15 in profit.Does Republic Services Have A Good Return On Equity?Arguably the easiest way to assess company's ROE is to compare it with the average in its industry. However, this method is only useful as a rough check, because companies do differ quite a bit within the same industry classification. As is clear from the image below, Republic Services has a better ROE than the average (13%) in the Commercial Services industry.roeThat's clearly a positive. Bear in mind, a high ROE doesn't always mean superior financial performance. A higher proportion of debt in a company's capital structure may also result in a high ROE, where the high debt levels could be a huge risk . To know the 2 risks we have identified for Republic Services visit our risks dashboard for free.How Does Debt Impact ROE?Most companies need money -- from somewhere -- to grow their profits. The cash for investment can come from prior year profits (retained earnings), issuing new shares, or borrowing. In the first and second cases, the ROE will reflect this use of cash for investment in the business. In the latter case, the debt used for growth will improve returns, but won't affect the total equity. Thus the use of debt can improve ROE, albeit along with extra risk in the case of stormy weather, metaphorically speaking.Story continuesRepublic Services' Debt And Its 15% ROERepublic Services does use a high amount of debt to increase returns. It has a debt to equity ratio of 1.21. While its ROE is pretty respectable, the amount of debt the company is carrying currently is not ideal. Investors should think carefully about how a company might perform if it was unable to borrow so easily, because credit markets do change over time.ConclusionReturn on equity is useful for comparing the quality of different businesses. A company that can achieve a high return on equity without debt could be considered a high quality business. All else being equal, a higher ROE is better.But ROE is just one piece of a bigger puzzle, since high quality businesses often trade on high multiples of earnings. The rate at which profits are likely to grow, relative to the expectations of profit growth reflected in the current price, must be considered, too. column4: Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE:RSG) Delivered A Better ROE Than Its Industry
column10: [Many investors are still learning about the various metrics that can be useful when analysing a stock. This article is for those who would like to learn about Return On Equity (ROE). We'll use ROE to examine Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE:RSG), by way of a worked example.ROE or return on equity is a useful tool to assess how effectively a company can generate returns on the investment it received from its shareholders. In short, ROE shows the profit each dollar generates with respect to its shareholder investments. See our latest analysis for Republic Services How Is ROE Calculated?Return on equity can be calculated by using the formula:Return on Equity = Net Profit (from continuing operations) ÷ Shareholders' EquitySo, based on the above formula, the ROE for Republic Services is:15% = US$1.5b ÷ US$9.9b (Based on the trailing twelve months to March 2023).The 'return' refers to a company's earnings over the last year. Another way to think of that is that for every $1 worth of equity, the company was able to earn $0.15 in profit.Does Republic Services Have A Good Return On Equity?Arguably the easiest way to assess company's ROE is to compare it with the average in its industry. However, this method is only useful as a rough check, because companies do differ quite a bit within the same industry classification. As is clear from the image below, Republic Services has a better ROE than the average (13%) in the Commercial Services industry.roeThat's clearly a positive. Bear in mind, a high ROE doesn't always mean superior financial performance. A higher proportion of debt in a company's capital structure may also result in a high ROE, where the high debt levels could be a huge risk . To know the 2 risks we have identified for Republic Services visit our risks dashboard for free.How Does Debt Impact ROE?Most companies need money -- from somewhere -- to grow their profits. The cash for investment can come from prior year profits (retained earnings), issuing new shares, or borrowing. In the first and second cases, the ROE will reflect this use of cash for investment in the business. In the latter case, the debt used for growth will improve returns, but won't affect the total equity. Thus the use of debt can improve ROE, albeit along with extra risk in the case of stormy weather, metaphorically speaking.Story continuesRepublic Services' Debt And Its 15% ROERepublic Services does use a high amount of debt to increase returns. Investors should think carefully about how a company might perform if it was unable to borrow so easily, because credit markets do change over time.ConclusionReturn on equity is useful for comparing the quality of different businesses. column4: Republic Services Opens Recycling Learning Center for Seattle Community

(NYSE: RSG), a leader in the environmental services industry, opened the Seattle region's first and only recycling education center at the company's recycling facility in Seattle. The Seattle Learning Center is designed to educate the community, including children, on proper recycling behaviors and offers visitors a behind-the-scenes look into recycling technology and the process for different materials. Educational displays detail the recycling process while visitors are able to try their hand at sorting on the miniature conveyor belt."Republic Services shares the Puget Sound region's strong commitment to sustainability and the environment," said Ryan Lawler, area president. "Education plays a critical role in the effectiveness of recycling programs, and we're proud to share our expertise through the Seattle Learning Center to increase the amount of recyclable materials collected in our community."The Learning Center's educational displays showcase recycling facts and best practices, and visually display the recycling process. Guided tours by recycling experts will help visitors learn how to properly recycle materials and the positive impact recycling has on the Puget Sound region. Visitors can climb into the cab of a Republic Services recycling truck, and tours conclude with a virtual view of the recycling center's operations. Free tours of Republic's Seattle Learning Center, located at 2733 3rd Avenue South, can be scheduled by emailing RecyclePNW@republicservices.com.Republic's Seattle Recycling Facility, located within Seattle's SoDo neighborhood, is one of the company's largest, contributing to the region's circular economy. Each year, the facility processes 200,000 tons of recyclables. Reuse of these materials has a climate benefit equal to planting 500,000 acres of forest or taking more than 85,000 gasoline-powered cars off the road.1Story continuesRepublic Services processes five million tons of recyclable materials annually through its 71 recycling facilities throughout the country. Visitors can climb into the cab of a Republic Services recycling truck, and tours conclude with a virtual view of the recycling center's operations. column4: Republic Services Completes Acquisition of GFL's Colorado and New Mexico Operations
column10: [PHOENIX, June 5, 2023 /PRNewswire/ -- Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG), a leader in the environmental services industry, today announced that it has completed its acquisition of GFL Environmental's Colorado and New Mexico operations. The vertically integrated operations include recycling, collection and disposal assets in four Colorado markets – Denver, Colorado Springs, Durango and Cañon City – as well as the Bloomfield, N.M., market."We look forward to delivering exceptional customer service to these new commercial and residential customers and welcome our new employees to the Republic team," said Ryan Lawler, area president. "This transaction reinforces our commitment to our Colorado and New Mexico communities."Republic Services offers the most complete set of products and services for its customers' environmental services needs. The company is committed to growing both organically and through strategic acquisitions that leverage its core capabilities and expertise while expanding the recycling, waste and environmental solutions provided to customers. About Republic ServicesRepublic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG) is a leader in the environmental services industry. Through its subsidiaries, the Company provides customers with the most complete set of products and services, including recycling, solid waste, special waste, hazardous waste, container rental and field services. Republic's industry-leading commitments to advance circularity, reduce emissions and decarbonize operations are helping deliver on its vision to partner with customers to create a more sustainable world. column4: Investors in Republic Services (NYSE:RSG) have seen stellar returns of 126% over the past five years
column10: [The worst result, after buying shares in a company (assuming no leverage), would be if you lose all the money you put in. But on the bright side, you can make far more than 100% on a really good stock. For example, the Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE:RSG) share price has soared 108% in the last half decade. Most would be very happy with that.With that in mind, it's worth seeing if the company's underlying fundamentals have been the driver of long term performance, or if there are some discrepancies. Check out our latest analysis for Republic Services There is no denying that markets are sometimes efficient, but prices do not always reflect underlying business performance. One flawed but reasonable way to assess how sentiment around a company has changed is to compare the earnings per share (EPS) with the share price.Over half a decade, Republic Services managed to grow its earnings per share at 3.9% a year. This EPS growth is lower than the 16% average annual increase in the share price. This suggests that market participants hold the company in higher regard, these days. That's not necessarily surprising considering the five-year track record of earnings growth.The company's earnings per share (over time) is depicted in the image below (click to see the exact numbers).earnings-per-share-growthWe consider it positive that insiders have made significant purchases in the last year. Even so, future earnings will be far more important to whether current shareholders make money. This free interactive report on Republic Services' earnings, revenue and cash flow is a great place to start, if you want to investigate the stock further.What About Dividends?As well as measuring the share price return, investors should also consider the total shareholder return (TSR). The TSR incorporates the value of any spin-offs or discounted capital raisings, along with any dividends, based on the assumption that the dividends are reinvested. Arguably, the TSR gives a more comprehensive picture of the return generated by a stock. We note that for Republic Services the TSR over the last 5 years was 126%, which is better than the share price return mentioned above. This is largely a result of its dividend payments!Story continuesA Different PerspectiveIt's good to see that Republic Services has rewarded shareholders with a total shareholder return of 7.3% in the last twelve months. Of course, that includes the dividend. However, that falls short of the 18% TSR per annum it has made for shareholders, each year, over five years. The pessimistic view would be that be that the stock has its best days behind it, but on the other hand the price might simply be moderating while the business itself continues to execute. I find it very interesting to look at share price over the long term as a proxy for business performance. But to truly gain insight, we need to consider other information, too. Consider risks, for instance. column10: [For Immediate ReleaseChicago, IL – May 23, 2023 – Today, Zacks Equity Research discusses Waste Management, Inc. WM, Republic Services, Inc. RSG and Clean Harbors, Inc. CLH.Industry: Waste RemovalLink: https://www.zacks.com/commentary/2098047/3-waste-removal-services-stocks-to-watch-amid-industry-challengesThe Zacks Waste Removal Services industry stands to benefit from the gradual resumption of business activities and reopening of the economy, which have led to increased waste production from industrial and commercial sectors. Government initiatives for sustainable waste management, increasing environmental awareness, rising population, rapid industrialization and urbanization, and growing adoption of advanced waste collection solutions are the other positives.Waste Management, Inc., Republic Services, Inc. and Clean Harbors, Inc. are some stocks likely to gain from the abovementioned factors.Industry DescriptionThe Zacks Waste Removal Services industry comprises companies engaged in the collection, transportation, treatment, disposal, inspection and regulation of any form of waste. The companies serve residential, municipal, commercial and industrial customers in the United States and internationally.Some industry participants provide non-hazardous solid waste collection, transfer, recycling, disposal, and energy services for small-container, large-container, municipal and residential, and energy services customers in the United States and Puerto Rico, while others provide waste management environmental services to residential, commercial, industrial, and municipal customers in North America. Some industry players operate as environmental infrastructure and solutions companies, providing water handling and recycling solutions.What's Shaping the Future of the Waste Removal Services Industry?A Healthy Demand Environment: The industry is mature, with growth coming from volume and price increases. Income has grown steadily over the past few years, enabling most industry players to pursue acquisitions and other investments.Story continuesReopening of Economic Activities Bodes Well: With the reopening of the economy and the resumption of business activities, waste generation is bound to increase, especially in the industrial and commercial sectors. The proper disposal of medical waste will always remain an utmost priority to curb the spread of infection. Increase in population, industrialization and urbanization should remain the key drivers of the industry as it leads to a significant rise in garbage and recycling. Also, the use of advanced collection and recycling solutions are expected to pick up pace. This should enhance business opportunities for waste management companies.Government initiatives as well as stringent rules and regulations to advance sustainable waste management mechanisms and put a check on illegal dumping are also expected to boost the industry.High Operating Costs a Woe: Waste management is a time-consuming and complex process. It requires higher capital and operating costs to manage waste collection vehicles, bins, and processing equipment along with a huge number of workers. Such high operational expenses are likely to keep the bottom line of the companies in this industrial cohort under pressure.Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Gloomy ProspectsThe Zacks Waste Removal Services industry, which is housed within the broader Zacks Business Services sector, currently carries a Zacks Industry Rank #189. This rank places it in the bottom 25% of more than 250 Zacks industries.The group’s Zacks Industry Rank, which is basically the average of the Zacks Rank of all member stocks, indicates dull near-term prospects. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperforms the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.Despite the cloudy prospects, we present a few stocks that investors can buy or retain given their sturdy potential. But before that let’s take a look at the industry’s recent stock market performance and its current valuation.Industry's PerformanceThe Zacks Waste Removal Services industry has outperformed the broader Zacks Business Services sector and the Zacks S&P 500 composite over the past year.The industry has gained 8.4% over this period against a 5.3% decline of the broader sector. The Zacks S&P 500 composite has risen 5.9% in the said time frame.Industry's Current ValuationOn the basis of EV-to-EBITDA (enterprise value to earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization), which is commonly used for valuing waste removal services stocks because of their high debt levels, the industry is currently trading at 14.39X compared with the S&P 500’s 12.69X and the sector’s 26.53X.Over the past five years, the industry has traded as high as 15.63X, as low as 8.57X and at the median of 11.97X.3 Waste Removal Services Stocks to Keep a Close Eye OnWe are presenting three stocks that carry a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) and are well-positioned to grow in the near term. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.Waste Management: Waste Management provides environmental solutions to residential, commercial, industrial, and municipal customers in the United States and Canada. WM’s top line has been benefiting from acquisition revenues and growth from yield. WM’s revenue growth for 2023 is expected to be between 4% and 5.5%, which includes organic revenue growth of nearly 5.5% from the collection and disposal business.The Zacks Consensus Estimate for WM’s 2023 EPS has improved 0.5% in the past 90 days. WM stock has gained 5.4% so far this year.Republic Services: Republic Services offers environmental services in the United States. The positive impact of acquisitions and internal growth has been aiding RSG’s top-line growth. RSG is focused on increasing its operational efficiency by shifting to compressed natural gas collection vehicles and converting rear-loading trucks to automated-side loaders to reduce costs and improve profitability.The Zacks Consensus Estimate for RSG’s 2023 EPS has improved 1.6% in the past 90 days. RSG stock has gained 12.5% so far this year.Clean Harbors: This Massachusetts-based company provides environmental and industrial services in the United States and internationally. Clean Harbors focuses on improving its efficiency and lowering operating costs through enhanced technology, process efficiencies and stringent cost management. It continues to make capital investments to enhance its service quality and comply with government and local regulations.Buyouts help the company expand its business across multiple lines of services. Consistency in rewarding shareholders through share buybacks boosts investor confidence and positively impacts earnings per share.For 2023, adjusted EBITDA is anticipated between $1.02 billion and $1.06 billion, up from the previous range of $1.01 billion and $1.05 billion. The rise reflects the company’s acquisition of Thompson Industrial Services.The Zacks Consensus Estimate for CLH’s 2023 EPS has moved up 2.1% in the past 90 days. column4: Republic Services Completes Acquisition of GFL's Colorado and New Mexico Operations
column10: [PHOENIX, June 5, 2023 /PRNewswire/ -- Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG), a leader in the environmental services industry, today announced that it has completed its acquisition of GFL Environmental's Colorado and New Mexico operations. The vertically integrated operations include recycling, collection and disposal assets in four Colorado markets – Denver, Colorado Springs, Durango and Cañon City – as well as the Bloomfield, N.M., market."We look forward to delivering exceptional customer service to these new commercial and residential customers and welcome our new employees to the Republic team," said Ryan Lawler, area president. "This transaction reinforces our commitment to our Colorado and New Mexico communities."Republic Services offers the most complete set of products and services for its customers' environmental services needs. The company is committed to growing both organically and through strategic acquisitions that leverage its core capabilities and expertise while expanding the recycling, waste and environmental solutions provided to customers. column4: Investors in Republic Services (NYSE:RSG) have seen stellar returns of 126% over the past five years
column10: [The worst result, after buying shares in a company (assuming no leverage), would be if you lose all the money you put in. But on the bright side, you can make far more than 100% on a really good stock. For example, the Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE:RSG) share price has soared 108% in the last half decade. Most would be very happy with that.With that in mind, it's worth seeing if the company's underlying fundamentals have been the driver of long term performance, or if there are some discrepancies. Check out our latest analysis for Republic Services There is no denying that markets are sometimes efficient, but prices do not always reflect underlying business performance. One flawed but reasonable way to assess how sentiment around a company has changed is to compare the earnings per share (EPS) with the share price.Over half a decade, Republic Services managed to grow its earnings per share at 3.9% a year. This EPS growth is lower than the 16% average annual increase in the share price. This suggests that market participants hold the company in higher regard, these days. That's not necessarily surprising considering the five-year track record of earnings growth.The company's earnings per share (over time) is depicted in the image below (click to see the exact numbers).earnings-per-share-growthWe consider it positive that insiders have made significant purchases in the last year. Even so, future earnings will be far more important to whether current shareholders make money. This free interactive report on Republic Services' earnings, revenue and cash flow is a great place to start, if you want to investigate the stock further.What About Dividends?As well as measuring the share price return, investors should also consider the total shareholder return (TSR). The TSR incorporates the value of any spin-offs or discounted capital raisings, along with any dividends, based on the assumption that the dividends are reinvested. Arguably, the TSR gives a more comprehensive picture of the return generated by a stock. We note that for Republic Services the TSR over the last 5 years was 126%, which is better than the share price return mentioned above. This is largely a result of its dividend payments!Story continuesA Different PerspectiveIt's good to see that Republic Services has rewarded shareholders with a total shareholder return of 7.3% in the last twelve months. Of course, that includes the dividend. However, that falls short of the 18% TSR per annum it has made for shareholders, each year, over five years. The pessimistic view would be that be that the stock has its best days behind it, but on the other hand the price might simply be moderating while the business itself continues to execute. I find it very interesting to look at share price over the long term as a proxy for business performance. But to truly gain insight, we need to consider other information, too. Consider risks, for instance. Zacks Industry Outlook Highlights Waste Management, Republic Services, and Clean Harbors
column10: [For Immediate ReleaseChicago, IL – May 23, 2023 – Today, Zacks Equity Research discusses Waste Management, Inc. WM, Republic Services, Inc. RSG and Clean Harbors, Inc. CLH.Industry: Waste RemovalLink: https://www.zacks.com/commentary/2098047/3-waste-removal-services-stocks-to-watch-amid-industry-challengesThe Zacks Waste Removal Services industry stands to benefit from the gradual resumption of business activities and reopening of the economy, which have led to increased waste production from industrial and commercial sectors. Government initiatives for sustainable waste management, increasing environmental awareness, rising population, rapid industrialization and urbanization, and growing adoption of advanced waste collection solutions are the other positives.Waste Management, Inc., Republic Services, Inc. and Clean Harbors, Inc. are some stocks likely to gain from the abovementioned factors.Industry DescriptionThe Zacks Waste Removal Services industry comprises companies engaged in the collection, transportation, treatment, disposal, inspection and regulation of any form of waste. The companies serve residential, municipal, commercial and industrial customers in the United States and internationally.Some industry participants provide non-hazardous solid waste collection, transfer, recycling, disposal, and energy services for small-container, large-container, municipal and residential, and energy services customers in the United States and Puerto Rico, while others provide waste management environmental services to residential, commercial, industrial, and municipal customers in North America. Some industry players operate as environmental infrastructure and solutions companies, providing water handling and recycling solutions.What's Shaping the Future of the Waste Removal Services Industry?A Healthy Demand Environment: The industry is mature, with growth coming from volume and price increases. Income has grown steadily over the past few years, enabling most industry players to pursue acquisitions and other investments.Story continuesReopening of Economic Activities Bodes Well: With the reopening of the economy and the resumption of business activities, waste generation is bound to increase, especially in the industrial and commercial sectors. The proper disposal of medical waste will always remain an utmost priority to curb the spread of infection. Increase in population, industrialization and urbanization should remain the key drivers of the industry as it leads to a significant rise in garbage and recycling. Also, the use of advanced collection and recycling solutions are expected to pick up pace. This should enhance business opportunities for waste management companies.Government initiatives as well as stringent rules and regulations to advance sustainable waste management mechanisms and put a check on illegal dumping are also expected to boost the industry.High Operating Costs a Woe: Waste management is a time-consuming and complex process. It requires higher capital and operating costs to manage waste collection vehicles, bins, and processing equipment along with a huge number of workers. Such high operational expenses are likely to keep the bottom line of the companies in this industrial cohort under pressure.Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Gloomy ProspectsThe Zacks Waste Removal Services industry, which is housed within the broader Zacks Business Services sector, currently carries a Zacks Industry Rank #189. This rank places it in the bottom 25% of more than 250 Zacks industries.The group’s Zacks Industry Rank, which is basically the average of the Zacks Rank of all member stocks, indicates dull near-term prospects. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperforms the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.Despite the cloudy prospects, we present a few stocks that investors can buy or retain given their sturdy potential. But before that let’s take a look at the industry’s recent stock market performance and its current valuation.Industry's PerformanceThe Zacks Waste Removal Services industry has outperformed the broader Zacks Business Services sector and the Zacks S&P 500 composite over the past year.The industry has gained 8.4% over this period against a 5.3% decline of the broader sector. The Zacks S&P 500 composite has risen 5.9% in the said time frame.Industry's Current ValuationOn the basis of EV-to-EBITDA (enterprise value to earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization), which is commonly used for valuing waste removal services stocks because of their high debt levels, the industry is currently trading at 14.39X compared with the S&P 500’s 12.69X and the sector’s 26.53X.Over the past five years, the industry has traded as high as 15.63X, as low as 8.57X and at the median of 11.97X.3 Waste Removal Services Stocks to Keep a Close Eye OnWe are presenting three stocks that carry a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) and are well-positioned to grow in the near term. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.Waste Management: Waste Management provides environmental solutions to residential, commercial, industrial, and municipal customers in the United States and Canada. WM’s top line has been benefiting from acquisition revenues and growth from yield. WM’s revenue growth for 2023 is expected to be between 4% and 5.5%, which includes organic revenue growth of nearly 5.5% from the collection and disposal business.The Zacks Consensus Estimate for WM’s 2023 EPS has improved 0.5% in the past 90 days. WM stock has gained 5.4% so far this year.Republic Services: Republic Services offers environmental services in the United States. The positive impact of acquisitions and internal growth has been aiding RSG’s top-line growth. RSG is focused on increasing its operational efficiency by shifting to compressed natural gas collection vehicles and converting rear-loading trucks to automated-side loaders to reduce costs and improve profitability.The Zacks Consensus Estimate for RSG’s 2023 EPS has improved 1.6% in the past 90 days. RSG stock has gained 12.5% so far this year.Clean Harbors: This Massachusetts-based company provides environmental and industrial services in the United States and internationally. Clean Harbors focuses on improving its efficiency and lowering operating costs through enhanced technology, process efficiencies and stringent cost management. It continues to make capital investments to enhance its service quality and comply with government and local regulations.Buyouts help the company expand its business across multiple lines of services. Consistency in rewarding shareholders through share buybacks boosts investor confidence and positively impacts earnings per share.For 2023, adjusted EBITDA is anticipated between $1.02 billion and $1.06 billion, up from the previous range of $1.01 billion and $1.05 billion. The rise reflects the company’s acquisition of Thompson Industrial Services.The Zacks Consensus Estimate for CLH’s 2023 EPS has moved up 2.1% in the past 90 days. Government initiatives for sustainable waste management, increasing environmental awareness, rising population, rapid industrialization and urbanization, and growing adoption of advanced waste collection solutions are the other positives.Waste Management, Inc., Republic Services, Inc. and Clean Harbors, Inc. are some stocks likely to gain from the abovementioned factors.Industry DescriptionThe Zacks Waste Removal Services industry comprises companies engaged in the collection, transportation, treatment, disposal, inspection and regulation of any form of waste. The companies serve residential, municipal, commercial and industrial customers in the United States and internationally.Some industry participants provide non-hazardous solid waste collection, transfer, recycling, disposal, and energy services for small-container, large-container, municipal and residential, and energy services customers in the United States and Puerto Rico, while others provide waste management environmental services to residential, commercial, industrial, and municipal customers in North America. Some industry players operate as environmental infrastructure and solutions companies, providing water handling and recycling solutions.What's Shaping the Future of the Waste Removal Services Industry?A Healthy Demand Environment: The industry is mature, with growth coming from volume and price increases. Income has grown steadily over the past few years, enabling most industry players to pursue acquisitions and other investments.Story continuesReopening of Economic Activities Bodes Well: With the reopening of the economy and the resumption of business activities, waste generation is bound to increase, especially in the industrial and commercial sectors. The proper disposal of medical waste will always remain an utmost priority to curb the spread of infection. Increase in population, industrialization and urbanization should remain the key drivers of the industry as it leads to a significant rise in garbage and recycling. Also, the use of advanced collection and recycling solutions are expected to pick up pace. This should enhance business opportunities for waste management companies.Government initiatives as well as stringent rules and regulations to advance sustainable waste management mechanisms and put a check on illegal dumping are also expected to boost the industry.High Operating Costs a Woe: Waste management is a time-consuming and complex process. It requires higher capital and operating costs to manage waste collection vehicles, bins, and processing equipment along with a huge number of workers. Such high operational expenses are likely to keep the bottom line of the companies in this industrial cohort under pressure.Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Gloomy ProspectsThe Zacks Waste Removal Services industry, which is housed within the broader Zacks Business Services sector, currently carries a Zacks Industry Rank #189. column10: [The worst result, after buying shares in a company (assuming no leverage), would be if you lose all the money you put in. But on the bright side, you can make far more than 100% on a really good stock. For example, the Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE:RSG) share price has soared 108% in the last half decade. Most would be very happy with that.With that in mind, it's worth seeing if the company's underlying fundamentals have been the driver of long term performance, or if there are some discrepancies. Check out our latest analysis for Republic Services There is no denying that markets are sometimes efficient, but prices do not always reflect underlying business performance. One flawed but reasonable way to assess how sentiment around a company has changed is to compare the earnings per share (EPS) with the share price.Over half a decade, Republic Services managed to grow its earnings per share at 3.9% a year. This EPS growth is lower than the 16% average annual increase in the share price. This suggests that market participants hold the company in higher regard, these days. That's not necessarily surprising considering the five-year track record of earnings growth.The company's earnings per share (over time) is depicted in the image below (click to see the exact numbers).earnings-per-share-growthWe consider it positive that insiders have made significant purchases in the last year. Even so, future earnings will be far more important to whether current shareholders make money. This free interactive report on Republic Services' earnings, revenue and cash flow is a great place to start, if you want to investigate the stock further.What About Dividends?As well as measuring the share price return, investors should also consider the total shareholder return (TSR). The TSR incorporates the value of any spin-offs or discounted capital raisings, along with any dividends, based on the assumption that the dividends are reinvested. Arguably, the TSR gives a more comprehensive picture of the return generated by a stock. We note that for Republic Services the TSR over the last 5 years was 126%, which is better than the share price return mentioned above. This is largely a result of its dividend payments!Story continuesA Different PerspectiveIt's good to see that Republic Services has rewarded shareholders with a total shareholder return of 7.3% in the last twelve months. Of course, that includes the dividend. However, that falls short of the 18% TSR per annum it has made for shareholders, each year, over five years. The pessimistic view would be that be that the stock has its best days behind it, but on the other hand the price might simply be moderating while the business itself continues to execute. I find it very interesting to look at share price over the long term as a proxy for business performance. But to truly gain insight, we need to consider other information, too. Consider risks, for instance. column4: Republic Services Completes Acquisition of GFL's Colorado and New Mexico Operations
column10: [PHOENIX, June 5, 2023 /PRNewswire/ -- Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG), a leader in the environmental services industry, today announced that it has completed its acquisition of GFL Environmental's Colorado and New Mexico operations. The vertically integrated operations include recycling, collection and disposal assets in four Colorado markets – Denver, Colorado Springs, Durango and Cañon City – as well as the Bloomfield, N.M., market."We look forward to delivering exceptional customer service to these new commercial and residential customers and welcome our new employees to the Republic team," said Ryan Lawler, area president. "This transaction reinforces our commitment to our Colorado and New Mexico communities."Republic Services offers the most complete set of products and services for its customers' environmental services needs. The company is committed to growing both organically and through strategic acquisitions that leverage its core capabilities and expertise while expanding the recycling, waste and environmental solutions provided to customers. About Republic ServicesRepublic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG) is a leader in the environmental services industry. Through its subsidiaries, the Company provides customers with the most complete set of products and services, including recycling, solid waste, special waste, hazardous waste, container rental and field services. Republic's industry-leading commitments to advance circularity, reduce emissions and decarbonize operations are helping deliver on its vision to partner with customers to create a more sustainable world. column4: Investors in Republic Services (NYSE:RSG) have seen stellar returns of 126% over the past five years
column10: [The worst result, after buying shares in a company (assuming no leverage), would be if you lose all the money you put in. But on the bright side, you can make far more than 100% on a really good stock. For example, the Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE:RSG) share price has soared 108% in the last half decade. Most would be very happy with that.With that in mind, it's worth seeing if the company's underlying fundamentals have been the driver of long term performance, or if there are some discrepancies. Check out our latest analysis for Republic Services There is no denying that markets are sometimes efficient, but prices do not always reflect underlying business performance. One flawed but reasonable way to assess how sentiment around a company has changed is to compare the earnings per share (EPS) with the share price.Over half a decade, Republic Services managed to grow its earnings per share at 3.9% a year. This EPS growth is lower than the 16% average annual increase in the share price. This suggests that market participants hold the company in higher regard, these days. That's not necessarily surprising considering the five-year track record of earnings growth.The company's earnings per share (over time) is depicted in the image below (click to see the exact numbers).earnings-per-share-growthWe consider it positive that insiders have made significant purchases in the last year. Even so, future earnings will be far more important to whether current shareholders make money. This free interactive report on Republic Services' earnings, revenue and cash flow is a great place to start, if you want to investigate the stock further.What About Dividends?As well as measuring the share price return, investors should also consider the total shareholder return (TSR). The TSR incorporates the value of any spin-offs or discounted capital raisings, along with any dividends, based on the assumption that the dividends are reinvested. Arguably, the TSR gives a more comprehensive picture of the return generated by a stock. We note that for Republic Services the TSR over the last 5 years was 126%, which is better than the share price return mentioned above. This is largely a result of its dividend payments!Story continuesA Different PerspectiveIt's good to see that Republic Services has rewarded shareholders with a total shareholder return of 7.3% in the last twelve months. Of course, that includes the dividend. However, that falls short of the 18% TSR per annum it has made for shareholders, each year, over five years. The pessimistic view would be that be that the stock has its best days behind it, but on the other hand the price might simply be moderating while the business itself continues to execute. I find it very interesting to look at share price over the long term as a proxy for business performance. But to truly gain insight, we need to consider other information, too. Consider risks, for instance. column4: 25 Cleanest Countries In the World In 2023
column10: [This article will look at the 25 cleanest countries in the world that are performing well on multiple environmental indicators like climate change mitigation, waste management, and air quality. We'll also discuss the continuously deteriorating air and environmental quality. If you want to skip the details, read 10 Cleanest Countries In The World In 2023. Grading the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023 is a subjective topic that requires a deep dive into their environment-related efforts. For instance, the Environmental Performance Index (EPI) offers a broad measure of environmental health and ecosystem vitality, ranking countries based on factors such as air and water quality, biodiversity, and climate and energy policies. The EPI, as of 2022, identified Denmark, Luxembourg, and Switzerland as the leading cleanest countries in the world.But these rankings might vary if we look at more specific indicators. For example, according to IQAir World Report 2022, Iceland has the highest air quality score, closely followed by Australia and New Zealand. Contrarily, these countries' wastewater treatment efforts are ranked 25th, 10th, and 15th, respectively. Moreover, cultural norms and attitudes towards cleanliness, waste management, and littering impact a country's cleanliness. Therefore, assessing a country's cleanliness is a subjective and complex topic, heavily reliant on the specific dimensions evaluated.Sustainability-Focused Waste Management CompaniesForward-thinking waste management companies like Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM), Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN), and Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) are continuously implementing efforts to make waste dumping sustainable. For instance, Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM) has goals like greenhouse gas emissions reduction and responsible waste dumping. The company has started producing renewable fuels by capturing gases released from its landfills and converting it into low-carbon fuel that supports a portion of its fleet. Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM) has a current market cap of $68.484 billion and it is one of the largest waste management companies in the USA. Story continuesMoreover, Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN), the third-largest solid waste management company in North America, that boasts a current market cap of $36.346 billion, increased the use of robotics in its recycling facility and consistently recycles 50% of its collected waste. Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN) also processes 50% of its leachate on-site and has completed the construction of two new leachate plants in 2022 to meet its groundwater safety goals. Arizona-based Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) is also focused on responsible environmental solutions for the residential sector. For instance, Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) has recorded a 9% reduction in its operational greenhouse gas emissions since 2017 and aims to drop this level to 10% by 2025. The company is also close to opening the country's first fully integrated plastic recycling facility in Las Vegas, named Polymer Center, by the end of this year, that'll aim to produce 100 million pounds of recycled plastic annually. Waste management companies are now focusing on recycling and clean energy sources more than ever. If you wish to be a part of these progressive mitigation efforts, read 11 Best Waste Management Stocks to Buy Now, and add more weight to your investment strategy. Which Is The No 1 Cleanest Country In The World?As per our recent analysis of multifaceted environmental parameters, Luxembourg is the cleanest country in the world in 2023. The country has exhibited an exemplary approach towards waste management, boasting an impressive recycling rate. Coupled with legislation and progressive public attitudes, this has facilitated a highly effective waste disposal system and minimized the country's environmental contamination. The wastewater treatment facilities in Luxembourg also display advanced technical acuity, achieving near-perfect filtration rates and significantly reducing aquatic pollution. This treatment proficiency and a remarkable level of infrastructure investment contribute to the nation's place among the top 10 cleanest countries in the world in 2023.Which Is The Cleanest Country In Asia?Japan's concerted efforts towards ecological sustainability confidently assert the country's distinction of being the cleanest country in Asia. Japan's initiatives focused on environmental preservation, particularly its commitment to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and developing renewable energy resources, have proven instrumental in setting new benchmarks for sustainable living. The country's environmentally-friendly policies are backed by robust infrastructure encouraging green practices and waste management.We have already covered 30 Least Polluted Countries in the World; give this detailed article a read to learn the planet's pollution dynamics. Which Is The Least Clean Country In The World?The Environmental Performance Index (EPI) 2022 report ranks India as the dirtiest country in the world, primarily due to its high population density, considerable vehicular congestion, and extensive biomass fuel usage. India's population growth, which is currently surpassing China, poses environmental challenges and calls for expansive mitigation efforts. For instance, urbanization and vehicular traffic explosion have badly impacted the country's air quality and propelled it to the bottom of the list. High emission levels from vehicles, combined with inadequate waste management, contribute to an alarming increase in air, water, and soil pollution. Additionally, India's reliance on biomass fuels, primarily in rural areas, further compounds the pollution problem. These fuels, including firewood, cow dung, and crop residues, emit substantial amounts of pollutants when burned. While India has tried to mitigate these issues, the magnitude of the challenges requires extensive environmental-friendly policies, justifying its ranking as the least clean country in the world per the EPI Report 2022.25 Cleanest Countries in the World in 202325 Cleanest Countries in the World in 2023Our Methodology To rank the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023, we relied on their air quality index, waste management system, and availability of wastewater treatment networks. To understand these crucial parameters, we referred to the Environmental Performance Index Report 2022 (collectively published by Yale and Columbia University), which analyzes 180 countries according to 40 environmental performance indicators. Our first step was to shortlist 25 countries with the best overall EPI score in 2022 (given that it is awarded based on extensive variables, these countries are doing well overall). Then, as solid waste management and wastewater treatment determine a country’s determination towards being ‘clean,’ we picked these two variables from the EPI Report and shortlisted 25 countries with the highest score in these categories. The report has awarded wastewater treatment scores to countries depending on what percentage of a nation’s wastewater undergoes at least some kind of treatment. For example, if a country’s whole population is connected to a sewerage system and all of the collected wastewater is treated, its score will be 100%. Similarly, the EPI Index measures a country’s waste management system according to its efforts to limit solid waste, recycling rates, and oceanic plastic pollution. So if a nation’s solid waste management score is 79%, it indicates its overall performance in these criteria collectively. For our 3rd key metric, i.e., air quality index, we referred to the IQAir World Air Quality Report 2022, which scores countries based on PM2.5 ranking. PM2.5 refers to atmospheric particulate matter (PM) with a diameter of less than 2.5 micrometers. column4: 25 Cleanest Countries In the World In 2023
column10: [This article will look at the 25 cleanest countries in the world that are performing well on multiple environmental indicators like climate change mitigation, waste management, and air quality. We'll also discuss the continuously deteriorating air and environmental quality. If you want to skip the details, read 10 Cleanest Countries In The World In 2023. Grading the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023 is a subjective topic that requires a deep dive into their environment-related efforts. For instance, the Environmental Performance Index (EPI) offers a broad measure of environmental health and ecosystem vitality, ranking countries based on factors such as air and water quality, biodiversity, and climate and energy policies. The EPI, as of 2022, identified Denmark, Luxembourg, and Switzerland as the leading cleanest countries in the world.But these rankings might vary if we look at more specific indicators. For example, according to IQAir World Report 2022, Iceland has the highest air quality score, closely followed by Australia and New Zealand. Contrarily, these countries' wastewater treatment efforts are ranked 25th, 10th, and 15th, respectively. Moreover, cultural norms and attitudes towards cleanliness, waste management, and littering impact a country's cleanliness. Therefore, assessing a country's cleanliness is a subjective and complex topic, heavily reliant on the specific dimensions evaluated.Sustainability-Focused Waste Management CompaniesForward-thinking waste management companies like Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM), Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN), and Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) are continuously implementing efforts to make waste dumping sustainable. For instance, Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM) has goals like greenhouse gas emissions reduction and responsible waste dumping. The company has started producing renewable fuels by capturing gases released from its landfills and converting it into low-carbon fuel that supports a portion of its fleet. Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM) has a current market cap of $68.484 billion and it is one of the largest waste management companies in the USA. Story continuesMoreover, Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN), the third-largest solid waste management company in North America, that boasts a current market cap of $36.346 billion, increased the use of robotics in its recycling facility and consistently recycles 50% of its collected waste. Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN) also processes 50% of its leachate on-site and has completed the construction of two new leachate plants in 2022 to meet its groundwater safety goals. Arizona-based Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) is also focused on responsible environmental solutions for the residential sector. For instance, Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) has recorded a 9% reduction in its operational greenhouse gas emissions since 2017 and aims to drop this level to 10% by 2025. The company is also close to opening the country's first fully integrated plastic recycling facility in Las Vegas, named Polymer Center, by the end of this year, that'll aim to produce 100 million pounds of recycled plastic annually. Waste management companies are now focusing on recycling and clean energy sources more than ever. If you wish to be a part of these progressive mitigation efforts, read 11 Best Waste Management Stocks to Buy Now, and add more weight to your investment strategy. Which Is The No 1 Cleanest Country In The World?As per our recent analysis of multifaceted environmental parameters, Luxembourg is the cleanest country in the world in 2023. The country has exhibited an exemplary approach towards waste management, boasting an impressive recycling rate. Coupled with legislation and progressive public attitudes, this has facilitated a highly effective waste disposal system and minimized the country's environmental contamination. The wastewater treatment facilities in Luxembourg also display advanced technical acuity, achieving near-perfect filtration rates and significantly reducing aquatic pollution. Japan's initiatives focused on environmental preservation, particularly its commitment to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and developing renewable energy resources, have proven instrumental in setting new benchmarks for sustainable living. The country's environmentally-friendly policies are backed by robust infrastructure encouraging green practices and waste management.We have already covered 30 Least Polluted Countries in the World; give this detailed article a read to learn the planet's pollution dynamics. Which Is The Least Clean Country In The World?The Environmental Performance Index (EPI) 2022 report ranks India as the dirtiest country in the world, primarily due to its high population density, considerable vehicular congestion, and extensive biomass fuel usage. India's population growth, which is currently surpassing China, poses environmental challenges and calls for expansive mitigation efforts. For instance, urbanization and vehicular traffic explosion have badly impacted the country's air quality and propelled it to the bottom of the list. High emission levels from vehicles, combined with inadequate waste management, contribute to an alarming increase in air, water, and soil pollution. Additionally, India's reliance on biomass fuels, primarily in rural areas, further compounds the pollution problem. These fuels, including firewood, cow dung, and crop residues, emit substantial amounts of pollutants when burned. While India has tried to mitigate these issues, the magnitude of the challenges requires extensive environmental-friendly policies, justifying its ranking as the least clean country in the world per the EPI Report 2022.25 Cleanest Countries in the World in 202325 Cleanest Countries in the World in 2023Our Methodology To rank the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023, we relied on their air quality index, waste management system, and availability of wastewater treatment networks. To understand these crucial parameters, we referred to the Environmental Performance Index Report 2022 (collectively published by Yale and Columbia University), which analyzes 180 countries according to 40 environmental performance indicators. Our first step was to shortlist 25 countries with the best overall EPI score in 2022 (given that it is awarded based on extensive variables, these countries are doing well overall). Then, as solid waste management and wastewater treatment determine a country’s determination towards being ‘clean,’ we picked these two variables from the EPI Report and shortlisted 25 countries with the highest score in these categories. The report has awarded wastewater treatment scores to countries depending on what percentage of a nation’s wastewater undergoes at least some kind of treatment. For example, if a country’s whole population is connected to a sewerage system and all of the collected wastewater is treated, its score will be 100%. Similarly, the EPI Index measures a country’s waste management system according to its efforts to limit solid waste, recycling rates, and oceanic plastic pollution. So if a nation’s solid waste management score is 79%, it indicates its overall performance in these criteria collectively. For our 3rd key metric, i.e., air quality index, we referred to the IQAir World Air Quality Report 2022, which scores countries based on PM2.5 ranking. PM2.5 refers to atmospheric particulate matter (PM) with a diameter of less than 2.5 micrometers. So if a place’s air has particulate matter between 0-12 μg/m³ (micrograms per cubic meter), it is considered good. Likewise, AQI of 12.1-34.5 μg/m³ is moderate, while a μg/m³ score of 55.5-150.4 is unhealthy. In short, the lower the 2.5PM rating, the better a country’s air quality will be.After listing these three variables individually for the top 25 countries, we averaged their scores to get composite rankings to present a broader perspective of their cleanliness levels. Based on our findings, here are the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023: 25. column4: 25 Cleanest Countries In the World In 2023
column10: [This article will look at the 25 cleanest countries in the world that are performing well on multiple environmental indicators like climate change mitigation, waste management, and air quality. We'll also discuss the continuously deteriorating air and environmental quality. If you want to skip the details, read 10 Cleanest Countries In The World In 2023. Grading the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023 is a subjective topic that requires a deep dive into their environment-related efforts. For instance, the Environmental Performance Index (EPI) offers a broad measure of environmental health and ecosystem vitality, ranking countries based on factors such as air and water quality, biodiversity, and climate and energy policies. The EPI, as of 2022, identified Denmark, Luxembourg, and Switzerland as the leading cleanest countries in the world.But these rankings might vary if we look at more specific indicators. For example, according to IQAir World Report 2022, Iceland has the highest air quality score, closely followed by Australia and New Zealand. Contrarily, these countries' wastewater treatment efforts are ranked 25th, 10th, and 15th, respectively. Moreover, cultural norms and attitudes towards cleanliness, waste management, and littering impact a country's cleanliness. Therefore, assessing a country's cleanliness is a subjective and complex topic, heavily reliant on the specific dimensions evaluated.Sustainability-Focused Waste Management CompaniesForward-thinking waste management companies like Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM), Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN), and Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) are continuously implementing efforts to make waste dumping sustainable. For instance, Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM) has goals like greenhouse gas emissions reduction and responsible waste dumping. The company has started producing renewable fuels by capturing gases released from its landfills and converting it into low-carbon fuel that supports a portion of its fleet. Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM) has a current market cap of $68.484 billion and it is one of the largest waste management companies in the USA. Story continuesMoreover, Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN), the third-largest solid waste management company in North America, that boasts a current market cap of $36.346 billion, increased the use of robotics in its recycling facility and consistently recycles 50% of its collected waste. Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN) also processes 50% of its leachate on-site and has completed the construction of two new leachate plants in 2022 to meet its groundwater safety goals. Arizona-based Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) is also focused on responsible environmental solutions for the residential sector. For instance, Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) has recorded a 9% reduction in its operational greenhouse gas emissions since 2017 and aims to drop this level to 10% by 2025. The company is also close to opening the country's first fully integrated plastic recycling facility in Las Vegas, named Polymer Center, by the end of this year, that'll aim to produce 100 million pounds of recycled plastic annually. Waste management companies are now focusing on recycling and clean energy sources more than ever. If you wish to be a part of these progressive mitigation efforts, read 11 Best Waste Management Stocks to Buy Now, and add more weight to your investment strategy. Which Is The No 1 Cleanest Country In The World?As per our recent analysis of multifaceted environmental parameters, Luxembourg is the cleanest country in the world in 2023. The country has exhibited an exemplary approach towards waste management, boasting an impressive recycling rate. Coupled with legislation and progressive public attitudes, this has facilitated a highly effective waste disposal system and minimized the country's environmental contamination. The wastewater treatment facilities in Luxembourg also display advanced technical acuity, achieving near-perfect filtration rates and significantly reducing aquatic pollution. This treatment proficiency and a remarkable level of infrastructure investment contribute to the nation's place among the top 10 cleanest countries in the world in 2023.Which Is The Cleanest Country In Asia?Japan's concerted efforts towards ecological sustainability confidently assert the country's distinction of being the cleanest country in Asia. Japan's initiatives focused on environmental preservation, particularly its commitment to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and developing renewable energy resources, have proven instrumental in setting new benchmarks for sustainable living. The country's environmentally-friendly policies are backed by robust infrastructure encouraging green practices and waste management.We have already covered 30 Least Polluted Countries in the World; give this detailed article a read to learn the planet's pollution dynamics. Which Is The Least Clean Country In The World?The Environmental Performance Index (EPI) 2022 report ranks India as the dirtiest country in the world, primarily due to its high population density, considerable vehicular congestion, and extensive biomass fuel usage. India's population growth, which is currently surpassing China, poses environmental challenges and calls for expansive mitigation efforts. For instance, urbanization and vehicular traffic explosion have badly impacted the country's air quality and propelled it to the bottom of the list. High emission levels from vehicles, combined with inadequate waste management, contribute to an alarming increase in air, water, and soil pollution. Additionally, India's reliance on biomass fuels, primarily in rural areas, further compounds the pollution problem. These fuels, including firewood, cow dung, and crop residues, emit substantial amounts of pollutants when burned. While India has tried to mitigate these issues, the magnitude of the challenges requires extensive environmental-friendly policies, justifying its ranking as the least clean country in the world per the EPI Report 2022.25 Cleanest Countries in the World in 202325 Cleanest Countries in the World in 2023Our Methodology To rank the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023, we relied on their air quality index, waste management system, and availability of wastewater treatment networks. To understand these crucial parameters, we referred to the Environmental Performance Index Report 2022 (collectively published by Yale and Columbia University), which analyzes 180 countries according to 40 environmental performance indicators. Our first step was to shortlist 25 countries with the best overall EPI score in 2022 (given that it is awarded based on extensive variables, these countries are doing well overall). Then, as solid waste management and wastewater treatment determine a country’s determination towards being ‘clean,’ we picked these two variables from the EPI Report and shortlisted 25 countries with the highest score in these categories. The report has awarded wastewater treatment scores to countries depending on what percentage of a nation’s wastewater undergoes at least some kind of treatment. For example, if a country’s whole population is connected to a sewerage system and all of the collected wastewater is treated, its score will be 100%. Similarly, the EPI Index measures a country’s waste management system according to its efforts to limit solid waste, recycling rates, and oceanic plastic pollution. So if a nation’s solid waste management score is 79%, it indicates its overall performance in these criteria collectively. For our 3rd key metric, i.e., air quality index, we referred to the IQAir World Air Quality Report 2022, which scores countries based on PM2.5 ranking. PM2.5 refers to atmospheric particulate matter (PM) with a diameter of less than 2.5 micrometers. So if a place’s air has particulate matter between 0-12 μg/m³ (micrograms per cubic meter), it is considered good. Likewise, AQI of 12.1-34.5 μg/m³ is moderate, while a μg/m³ score of 55.5-150.4 is unhealthy. In short, the lower the 2.5PM rating, the better a country’s air quality will be.After listing these three variables individually for the top 25 countries, we averaged their scores to get composite rankings to present a broader perspective of their cleanliness levels. Based on our findings, here are the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023: 25. Cyprus Composite Ranking: 25 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 15.6 Waste Management Score: 58.9%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 50%  Our list of cleanest countries in the world in 2023 starts with Cyprus, owing to its moderate wastewater treatment system and solid waste management efforts. Although the country's air quality index is 15.6 (PM2.5 μg/m³ being the best score), its moderate waste system is commendable. Also, stringent regulations on emissions combined with a transition towards renewable energy have significantly improved the country's air quality.24. UNESCO's sustainability index also applauds Croatia's dedication to maintaining pristine ecosystems.23. This success can be attributed to the country's rigorous policies on waste management, its substantial investment in renewable energy, and the adoption of eco-friendly practices by the population.22. Slovakia Composite Ranking: 22 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 14.5 Waste Management Score: 62.2%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 44.7%With an impressive waste management score of 62.2%, Slovakia has cemented its place on the list of cleanest places to live in 2023. Data from the Environmental Performance Index shows the country's solid environmental policies, along with a focus on reducing air and water pollution.21. Malta Composite Ranking: 21 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 11.7  Waste Management Score: 63.5%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 14.9% Although Malta's wastewater treatment system isn't as commendable as others on our list, its solid waste management strategies and air quality index make it one of the cleanest places to live in 2023. With an aim to become the leader in green energy deployment, Malta's transition to renewable resources has notably reduced pollution. 20. Japan Composite Ranking: 20 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 9.1  Waste Management Score: 52.8%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 74.8% Japan is the cleanest country in Asia because of the country's culture and modern infrastructure. In 2023, Japan firmly established itself amongst the world's cleanest nations, boasting a wastewater treatment index of 74.8%. Alongside comprehensive recycling and waste management programs, Japan also demonstrates leadership in energy conservation and green urban planning that further augment its reputation for environmental sustainability. 19. Belgium Composite Ranking: 19 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 10.8 Waste Management Score: 68%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 68.2% Belgium exemplifies exceptional environmental health, as demonstrated by the EPI Report 2022, which reviews 180 nations based on 40 performance indicators. Belgium's ranking evidences its commitment to mitigating pollution and managing solid waste. 18. Czech Republic Composite Ranking: 18 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 13.4 Waste Management Score: 74.9%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 61.5% The Czech Republic is also recognized as one of the world's cleanest countries, as confirmed by the Environmental Performance Index (EPI) Report 2022. The EPI Report ranked France amongst the top-performing nations because of its air quality, waste management, and climate change adaptation. 17. France Composite Ranking: 17 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 11.5  Waste Management Score: 63.8%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 88% France is one of the cleanest countries in the world largely due to its exceptional wastewater treatment, which is scored 88% as of current. Moreover, the country's solid waste management system scores 63.8% and shows the French government's concerted efforts to prioritize recycling and minimize landfill usage.16. Slovenia Composite Ranking: 16 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 15.1  Waste Management Score: 66.7%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 92.2% Slovenia has achieved a commendable wastewater treatment score of 92.2%, indicating highly efficient removal and neutralization of pollutants from water. Also, the nation's solid waste management rating of 66.7% demonstrates its smart waste reduction, segregation, and recycling which contribute to its low environmental impact and outstanding cleanliness.15. Latvia Composite Ranking: 15 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 10.1  Waste Management Score: 63%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 90.7% As of 2023, Latvia has one of the best national-level performances in wastewater treatment, marked by a score of 90.7%, which shows its repurposing of water resources and controlling pollution. Coupled with a solid waste management rating of 63%, Latvia has a solid reputation for environmental cleanliness.14. Its highly efficient wastewater management system, which records a 70.40% treatment score, further attests to the country's stringent environmental protection standards. 12.
