25 Cleanest Countries In the World In 2023
column10: [This article will look at the 25 cleanest countries in the world that are performing well on multiple environmental indicators like climate change mitigation, waste management, and air quality. We'll also discuss the continuously deteriorating air and environmental quality. If you want to skip the details, read 10 Cleanest Countries In The World In 2023. Grading the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023 is a subjective topic that requires a deep dive into their environment-related efforts. For instance, the Environmental Performance Index (EPI) offers a broad measure of environmental health and ecosystem vitality, ranking countries based on factors such as air and water quality, biodiversity, and climate and energy policies. The EPI, as of 2022, identified Denmark, Luxembourg, and Switzerland as the leading cleanest countries in the world.But these rankings might vary if we look at more specific indicators. For example, according to IQAir World Report 2022, Iceland has the highest air quality score, closely followed by Australia and New Zealand. Contrarily, these countries' wastewater treatment efforts are ranked 25th, 10th, and 15th, respectively. Moreover, cultural norms and attitudes towards cleanliness, waste management, and littering impact a country's cleanliness. Therefore, assessing a country's cleanliness is a subjective and complex topic, heavily reliant on the specific dimensions evaluated.Sustainability-Focused Waste Management CompaniesForward-thinking waste management companies like Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM), Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN), and Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) are continuously implementing efforts to make waste dumping sustainable. For instance, Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM) has goals like greenhouse gas emissions reduction and responsible waste dumping. The company has started producing renewable fuels by capturing gases released from its landfills and converting it into low-carbon fuel that supports a portion of its fleet. Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM) has a current market cap of $68.484 billion and it is one of the largest waste management companies in the USA. Story continuesMoreover, Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN), the third-largest solid waste management company in North America, that boasts a current market cap of $36.346 billion, increased the use of robotics in its recycling facility and consistently recycles 50% of its collected waste. Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN) also processes 50% of its leachate on-site and has completed the construction of two new leachate plants in 2022 to meet its groundwater safety goals. Arizona-based Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) is also focused on responsible environmental solutions for the residential sector. For instance, Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) has recorded a 9% reduction in its operational greenhouse gas emissions since 2017 and aims to drop this level to 10% by 2025. The company is also close to opening the country's first fully integrated plastic recycling facility in Las Vegas, named Polymer Center, by the end of this year, that'll aim to produce 100 million pounds of recycled plastic annually. Waste management companies are now focusing on recycling and clean energy sources more than ever. If you wish to be a part of these progressive mitigation efforts, read 11 Best Waste Management Stocks to Buy Now, and add more weight to your investment strategy. Which Is The No 1 Cleanest Country In The World?As per our recent analysis of multifaceted environmental parameters, Luxembourg is the cleanest country in the world in 2023. The country has exhibited an exemplary approach towards waste management, boasting an impressive recycling rate. Coupled with legislation and progressive public attitudes, this has facilitated a highly effective waste disposal system and minimized the country's environmental contamination. The wastewater treatment facilities in Luxembourg also display advanced technical acuity, achieving near-perfect filtration rates and significantly reducing aquatic pollution. This treatment proficiency and a remarkable level of infrastructure investment contribute to the nation's place among the top 10 cleanest countries in the world in 2023.Which Is The Cleanest Country In Asia?Japan's concerted efforts towards ecological sustainability confidently assert the country's distinction of being the cleanest country in Asia. Japan's initiatives focused on environmental preservation, particularly its commitment to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and developing renewable energy resources, have proven instrumental in setting new benchmarks for sustainable living. The country's environmentally-friendly policies are backed by robust infrastructure encouraging green practices and waste management.We have already covered 30 Least Polluted Countries in the World; give this detailed article a read to learn the planet's pollution dynamics. Which Is The Least Clean Country In The World?The Environmental Performance Index (EPI) 2022 report ranks India as the dirtiest country in the world, primarily due to its high population density, considerable vehicular congestion, and extensive biomass fuel usage. India's population growth, which is currently surpassing China, poses environmental challenges and calls for expansive mitigation efforts. For instance, urbanization and vehicular traffic explosion have badly impacted the country's air quality and propelled it to the bottom of the list. High emission levels from vehicles, combined with inadequate waste management, contribute to an alarming increase in air, water, and soil pollution. Additionally, India's reliance on biomass fuels, primarily in rural areas, further compounds the pollution problem. These fuels, including firewood, cow dung, and crop residues, emit substantial amounts of pollutants when burned. While India has tried to mitigate these issues, the magnitude of the challenges requires extensive environmental-friendly policies, justifying its ranking as the least clean country in the world per the EPI Report 2022.25 Cleanest Countries in the World in 202325 Cleanest Countries in the World in 2023Our Methodology To rank the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023, we relied on their air quality index, waste management system, and availability of wastewater treatment networks. To understand these crucial parameters, we referred to the Environmental Performance Index Report 2022 (collectively published by Yale and Columbia University), which analyzes 180 countries according to 40 environmental performance indicators. Our first step was to shortlist 25 countries with the best overall EPI score in 2022 (given that it is awarded based on extensive variables, these countries are doing well overall). Then, as solid waste management and wastewater treatment determine a country’s determination towards being ‘clean,’ we picked these two variables from the EPI Report and shortlisted 25 countries with the highest score in these categories. The report has awarded wastewater treatment scores to countries depending on what percentage of a nation’s wastewater undergoes at least some kind of treatment. For example, if a country’s whole population is connected to a sewerage system and all of the collected wastewater is treated, its score will be 100%. Similarly, the EPI Index measures a country’s waste management system according to its efforts to limit solid waste, recycling rates, and oceanic plastic pollution. So if a nation’s solid waste management score is 79%, it indicates its overall performance in these criteria collectively. For our 3rd key metric, i.e., air quality index, we referred to the IQAir World Air Quality Report 2022, which scores countries based on PM2.5 ranking. PM2.5 refers to atmospheric particulate matter (PM) with a diameter of less than 2.5 micrometers. So if a place’s air has particulate matter between 0-12 μg/m³ (micrograms per cubic meter), it is considered good. Likewise, AQI of 12.1-34.5 μg/m³ is moderate, while a μg/m³ score of 55.5-150.4 is unhealthy. In short, the lower the 2.5PM rating, the better a country’s air quality will be.After listing these three variables individually for the top 25 countries, we averaged their scores to get composite rankings to present a broader perspective of their cleanliness levels. Based on our findings, here are the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023: 25. Also, stringent regulations on emissions combined with a transition towards renewable energy have significantly improved the country's air quality.24. UNESCO's sustainability index also applauds Croatia's dedication to maintaining pristine ecosystems.23. This success can be attributed to the country's rigorous policies on waste management, its substantial investment in renewable energy, and the adoption of eco-friendly practices by the population.22. Slovakia Composite Ranking: 22 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 14.5 Waste Management Score: 62.2%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 44.7%With an impressive waste management score of 62.2%, Slovakia has cemented its place on the list of cleanest places to live in 2023. Data from the Environmental Performance Index shows the country's solid environmental policies, along with a focus on reducing air and water pollution.21. Malta Composite Ranking: 21 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 11.7  Waste Management Score: 63.5%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 14.9% Although Malta's wastewater treatment system isn't as commendable as others on our list, its solid waste management strategies and air quality index make it one of the cleanest places to live in 2023. With an aim to become the leader in green energy deployment, Malta's transition to renewable resources has notably reduced pollution. 20. Japan Composite Ranking: 20 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 9.1  Waste Management Score: 52.8%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 74.8% Japan is the cleanest country in Asia because of the country's culture and modern infrastructure. In 2023, Japan firmly established itself amongst the world's cleanest nations, boasting a wastewater treatment index of 74.8%. Alongside comprehensive recycling and waste management programs, Japan also demonstrates leadership in energy conservation and green urban planning that further augment its reputation for environmental sustainability. 19. Belgium Composite Ranking: 19 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 10.8 Waste Management Score: 68%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 68.2% Belgium exemplifies exceptional environmental health, as demonstrated by the EPI Report 2022, which reviews 180 nations based on 40 performance indicators. Belgium's ranking evidences its commitment to mitigating pollution and managing solid waste. 18. Czech Republic Composite Ranking: 18 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 13.4 Waste Management Score: 74.9%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 61.5% The Czech Republic is also recognized as one of the world's cleanest countries, as confirmed by the Environmental Performance Index (EPI) Report 2022. The EPI Report ranked France amongst the top-performing nations because of its air quality, waste management, and climate change adaptation. 17. 25 Cleanest Countries In the World In 2023
column10: [This article will look at the 25 cleanest countries in the world that are performing well on multiple environmental indicators like climate change mitigation, waste management, and air quality. We'll also discuss the continuously deteriorating air and environmental quality. If you want to skip the details, read 10 Cleanest Countries In The World In 2023. Grading the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023 is a subjective topic that requires a deep dive into their environment-related efforts. For instance, the Environmental Performance Index (EPI) offers a broad measure of environmental health and ecosystem vitality, ranking countries based on factors such as air and water quality, biodiversity, and climate and energy policies. The EPI, as of 2022, identified Denmark, Luxembourg, and Switzerland as the leading cleanest countries in the world.But these rankings might vary if we look at more specific indicators. For example, according to IQAir World Report 2022, Iceland has the highest air quality score, closely followed by Australia and New Zealand. Contrarily, these countries' wastewater treatment efforts are ranked 25th, 10th, and 15th, respectively. Moreover, cultural norms and attitudes towards cleanliness, waste management, and littering impact a country's cleanliness. Therefore, assessing a country's cleanliness is a subjective and complex topic, heavily reliant on the specific dimensions evaluated.Sustainability-Focused Waste Management CompaniesForward-thinking waste management companies like Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM), Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN), and Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) are continuously implementing efforts to make waste dumping sustainable. For instance, Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM) has goals like greenhouse gas emissions reduction and responsible waste dumping. The company has started producing renewable fuels by capturing gases released from its landfills and converting it into low-carbon fuel that supports a portion of its fleet. Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM) has a current market cap of $68.484 billion and it is one of the largest waste management companies in the USA. Story continuesMoreover, Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN), the third-largest solid waste management company in North America, that boasts a current market cap of $36.346 billion, increased the use of robotics in its recycling facility and consistently recycles 50% of its collected waste. Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN) also processes 50% of its leachate on-site and has completed the construction of two new leachate plants in 2022 to meet its groundwater safety goals. Arizona-based Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) is also focused on responsible environmental solutions for the residential sector. For instance, Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) has recorded a 9% reduction in its operational greenhouse gas emissions since 2017 and aims to drop this level to 10% by 2025. The company is also close to opening the country's first fully integrated plastic recycling facility in Las Vegas, named Polymer Center, by the end of this year, that'll aim to produce 100 million pounds of recycled plastic annually. Waste management companies are now focusing on recycling and clean energy sources more than ever. If you wish to be a part of these progressive mitigation efforts, read 11 Best Waste Management Stocks to Buy Now, and add more weight to your investment strategy. Which Is The No 1 Cleanest Country In The World?As per our recent analysis of multifaceted environmental parameters, Luxembourg is the cleanest country in the world in 2023. The country has exhibited an exemplary approach towards waste management, boasting an impressive recycling rate. Coupled with legislation and progressive public attitudes, this has facilitated a highly effective waste disposal system and minimized the country's environmental contamination. The wastewater treatment facilities in Luxembourg also display advanced technical acuity, achieving near-perfect filtration rates and significantly reducing aquatic pollution. This treatment proficiency and a remarkable level of infrastructure investment contribute to the nation's place among the top 10 cleanest countries in the world in 2023.Which Is The Cleanest Country In Asia?Japan's concerted efforts towards ecological sustainability confidently assert the country's distinction of being the cleanest country in Asia. Japan's initiatives focused on environmental preservation, particularly its commitment to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and developing renewable energy resources, have proven instrumental in setting new benchmarks for sustainable living. The country's environmentally-friendly policies are backed by robust infrastructure encouraging green practices and waste management.We have already covered 30 Least Polluted Countries in the World; give this detailed article a read to learn the planet's pollution dynamics. Which Is The Least Clean Country In The World?The Environmental Performance Index (EPI) 2022 report ranks India as the dirtiest country in the world, primarily due to its high population density, considerable vehicular congestion, and extensive biomass fuel usage. India's population growth, which is currently surpassing China, poses environmental challenges and calls for expansive mitigation efforts. For instance, urbanization and vehicular traffic explosion have badly impacted the country's air quality and propelled it to the bottom of the list. High emission levels from vehicles, combined with inadequate waste management, contribute to an alarming increase in air, water, and soil pollution. Additionally, India's reliance on biomass fuels, primarily in rural areas, further compounds the pollution problem. These fuels, including firewood, cow dung, and crop residues, emit substantial amounts of pollutants when burned. While India has tried to mitigate these issues, the magnitude of the challenges requires extensive environmental-friendly policies, justifying its ranking as the least clean country in the world per the EPI Report 2022.25 Cleanest Countries in the World in 202325 Cleanest Countries in the World in 2023Our Methodology To rank the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023, we relied on their air quality index, waste management system, and availability of wastewater treatment networks. To understand these crucial parameters, we referred to the Environmental Performance Index Report 2022 (collectively published by Yale and Columbia University), which analyzes 180 countries according to 40 environmental performance indicators. Our first step was to shortlist 25 countries with the best overall EPI score in 2022 (given that it is awarded based on extensive variables, these countries are doing well overall). Then, as solid waste management and wastewater treatment determine a country’s determination towards being ‘clean,’ we picked these two variables from the EPI Report and shortlisted 25 countries with the highest score in these categories. The report has awarded wastewater treatment scores to countries depending on what percentage of a nation’s wastewater undergoes at least some kind of treatment. For example, if a country’s whole population is connected to a sewerage system and all of the collected wastewater is treated, its score will be 100%. Similarly, the EPI Index measures a country’s waste management system according to its efforts to limit solid waste, recycling rates, and oceanic plastic pollution. So if a nation’s solid waste management score is 79%, it indicates its overall performance in these criteria collectively. For our 3rd key metric, i.e., air quality index, we referred to the IQAir World Air Quality Report 2022, which scores countries based on PM2.5 ranking. PM2.5 refers to atmospheric particulate matter (PM) with a diameter of less than 2.5 micrometers. So if a place’s air has particulate matter between 0-12 μg/m³ (micrograms per cubic meter), it is considered good. Likewise, AQI of 12.1-34.5 μg/m³ is moderate, while a μg/m³ score of 55.5-150.4 is unhealthy. In short, the lower the 2.5PM rating, the better a country’s air quality will be.After listing these three variables individually for the top 25 countries, we averaged their scores to get composite rankings to present a broader perspective of their cleanliness levels. Based on our findings, here are the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023: 25. UNESCO's sustainability index also applauds Croatia's dedication to maintaining pristine ecosystems.23. This success can be attributed to the country's rigorous policies on waste management, its substantial investment in renewable energy, and the adoption of eco-friendly practices by the population.22. Slovakia Composite Ranking: 22 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 14.5 Waste Management Score: 62.2%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 44.7%With an impressive waste management score of 62.2%, Slovakia has cemented its place on the list of cleanest places to live in 2023. Data from the Environmental Performance Index shows the country's solid environmental policies, along with a focus on reducing air and water pollution.21. Malta Composite Ranking: 21 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 11.7  Waste Management Score: 63.5%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 14.9% Although Malta's wastewater treatment system isn't as commendable as others on our list, its solid waste management strategies and air quality index make it one of the cleanest places to live in 2023. With an aim to become the leader in green energy deployment, Malta's transition to renewable resources has notably reduced pollution. 20. Japan Composite Ranking: 20 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 9.1  Waste Management Score: 52.8%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 74.8% Japan is the cleanest country in Asia because of the country's culture and modern infrastructure. In 2023, Japan firmly established itself amongst the world's cleanest nations, boasting a wastewater treatment index of 74.8%. Alongside comprehensive recycling and waste management programs, Japan also demonstrates leadership in energy conservation and green urban planning that further augment its reputation for environmental sustainability. 19. Belgium Composite Ranking: 19 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 10.8 Waste Management Score: 68%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 68.2% Belgium exemplifies exceptional environmental health, as demonstrated by the EPI Report 2022, which reviews 180 nations based on 40 performance indicators. Belgium's ranking evidences its commitment to mitigating pollution and managing solid waste. 18. Czech Republic Composite Ranking: 18 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 13.4 Waste Management Score: 74.9%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 61.5% The Czech Republic is also recognized as one of the world's cleanest countries, as confirmed by the Environmental Performance Index (EPI) Report 2022. The EPI Report ranked France amongst the top-performing nations because of its air quality, waste management, and climate change adaptation. 17. Moreover, the country's solid waste management system scores 63.8% and shows the French government's concerted efforts to prioritize recycling and minimize landfill usage.16. Slovenia Composite Ranking: 16 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 15.1  Waste Management Score: 66.7%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 92.2% Slovenia has achieved a commendable wastewater treatment score of 92.2%, indicating highly efficient removal and neutralization of pollutants from water. Plus, a wastewater treatment efficacy score of 79.9% underscores NZ's advanced waste management practices. 13. column4: 25 Cleanest Countries In the World In 2023
column10: [This article will look at the 25 cleanest countries in the world that are performing well on multiple environmental indicators like climate change mitigation, waste management, and air quality. We'll also discuss the continuously deteriorating air and environmental quality. If you want to skip the details, read 10 Cleanest Countries In The World In 2023. Grading the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023 is a subjective topic that requires a deep dive into their environment-related efforts. For instance, the Environmental Performance Index (EPI) offers a broad measure of environmental health and ecosystem vitality, ranking countries based on factors such as air and water quality, biodiversity, and climate and energy policies. The EPI, as of 2022, identified Denmark, Luxembourg, and Switzerland as the leading cleanest countries in the world.But these rankings might vary if we look at more specific indicators. For example, according to IQAir World Report 2022, Iceland has the highest air quality score, closely followed by Australia and New Zealand. Contrarily, these countries' wastewater treatment efforts are ranked 25th, 10th, and 15th, respectively. Moreover, cultural norms and attitudes towards cleanliness, waste management, and littering impact a country's cleanliness. Therefore, assessing a country's cleanliness is a subjective and complex topic, heavily reliant on the specific dimensions evaluated.Sustainability-Focused Waste Management CompaniesForward-thinking waste management companies like Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM), Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN), and Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) are continuously implementing efforts to make waste dumping sustainable. For instance, Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM) has goals like greenhouse gas emissions reduction and responsible waste dumping. The company has started producing renewable fuels by capturing gases released from its landfills and converting it into low-carbon fuel that supports a portion of its fleet. Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM) has a current market cap of $68.484 billion and it is one of the largest waste management companies in the USA. Story continuesMoreover, Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN), the third-largest solid waste management company in North America, that boasts a current market cap of $36.346 billion, increased the use of robotics in its recycling facility and consistently recycles 50% of its collected waste. Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN) also processes 50% of its leachate on-site and has completed the construction of two new leachate plants in 2022 to meet its groundwater safety goals. Arizona-based Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) is also focused on responsible environmental solutions for the residential sector. For instance, Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) has recorded a 9% reduction in its operational greenhouse gas emissions since 2017 and aims to drop this level to 10% by 2025. The company is also close to opening the country's first fully integrated plastic recycling facility in Las Vegas, named Polymer Center, by the end of this year, that'll aim to produce 100 million pounds of recycled plastic annually. Waste management companies are now focusing on recycling and clean energy sources more than ever. If you wish to be a part of these progressive mitigation efforts, read 11 Best Waste Management Stocks to Buy Now, and add more weight to your investment strategy. Which Is The No 1 Cleanest Country In The World?As per our recent analysis of multifaceted environmental parameters, Luxembourg is the cleanest country in the world in 2023. The country has exhibited an exemplary approach towards waste management, boasting an impressive recycling rate. Coupled with legislation and progressive public attitudes, this has facilitated a highly effective waste disposal system and minimized the country's environmental contamination. The wastewater treatment facilities in Luxembourg also display advanced technical acuity, achieving near-perfect filtration rates and significantly reducing aquatic pollution. This treatment proficiency and a remarkable level of infrastructure investment contribute to the nation's place among the top 10 cleanest countries in the world in 2023.Which Is The Cleanest Country In Asia?Japan's concerted efforts towards ecological sustainability confidently assert the country's distinction of being the cleanest country in Asia. Japan's initiatives focused on environmental preservation, particularly its commitment to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and developing renewable energy resources, have proven instrumental in setting new benchmarks for sustainable living. The country's environmentally-friendly policies are backed by robust infrastructure encouraging green practices and waste management.We have already covered 30 Least Polluted Countries in the World; give this detailed article a read to learn the planet's pollution dynamics. Which Is The Least Clean Country In The World?The Environmental Performance Index (EPI) 2022 report ranks India as the dirtiest country in the world, primarily due to its high population density, considerable vehicular congestion, and extensive biomass fuel usage. India's population growth, which is currently surpassing China, poses environmental challenges and calls for expansive mitigation efforts. For instance, urbanization and vehicular traffic explosion have badly impacted the country's air quality and propelled it to the bottom of the list. High emission levels from vehicles, combined with inadequate waste management, contribute to an alarming increase in air, water, and soil pollution. Additionally, India's reliance on biomass fuels, primarily in rural areas, further compounds the pollution problem. These fuels, including firewood, cow dung, and crop residues, emit substantial amounts of pollutants when burned. While India has tried to mitigate these issues, the magnitude of the challenges requires extensive environmental-friendly policies, justifying its ranking as the least clean country in the world per the EPI Report 2022.25 Cleanest Countries in the World in 202325 Cleanest Countries in the World in 2023Our Methodology To rank the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023, we relied on their air quality index, waste management system, and availability of wastewater treatment networks. To understand these crucial parameters, we referred to the Environmental Performance Index Report 2022 (collectively published by Yale and Columbia University), which analyzes 180 countries according to 40 environmental performance indicators. Our first step was to shortlist 25 countries with the best overall EPI score in 2022 (given that it is awarded based on extensive variables, these countries are doing well overall). Then, as solid waste management and wastewater treatment determine a country’s determination towards being ‘clean,’ we picked these two variables from the EPI Report and shortlisted 25 countries with the highest score in these categories. The report has awarded wastewater treatment scores to countries depending on what percentage of a nation’s wastewater undergoes at least some kind of treatment. For example, if a country’s whole population is connected to a sewerage system and all of the collected wastewater is treated, its score will be 100%. Similarly, the EPI Index measures a country’s waste management system according to its efforts to limit solid waste, recycling rates, and oceanic plastic pollution. So if a nation’s solid waste management score is 79%, it indicates its overall performance in these criteria collectively. For our 3rd key metric, i.e., air quality index, we referred to the IQAir World Air Quality Report 2022, which scores countries based on PM2.5 ranking. PM2.5 refers to atmospheric particulate matter (PM) with a diameter of less than 2.5 micrometers. So if a place’s air has particulate matter between 0-12 μg/m³ (micrograms per cubic meter), it is considered good. Likewise, AQI of 12.1-34.5 μg/m³ is moderate, while a μg/m³ score of 55.5-150.4 is unhealthy. In short, the lower the 2.5PM rating, the better a country’s air quality will be.After listing these three variables individually for the top 25 countries, we averaged their scores to get composite rankings to present a broader perspective of their cleanliness levels. Based on our findings, here are the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023: 25. This success can be attributed to the country's rigorous policies on waste management, its substantial investment in renewable energy, and the adoption of eco-friendly practices by the population.22. Malta Composite Ranking: 21 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 11.7  Waste Management Score: 63.5%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 14.9% Although Malta's wastewater treatment system isn't as commendable as others on our list, its solid waste management strategies and air quality index make it one of the cleanest places to live in 2023. With an aim to become the leader in green energy deployment, Malta's transition to renewable resources has notably reduced pollution. 20. Japan Composite Ranking: 20 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 9.1  Waste Management Score: 52.8%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 74.8% Japan is the cleanest country in Asia because of the country's culture and modern infrastructure. In 2023, Japan firmly established itself amongst the world's cleanest nations, boasting a wastewater treatment index of 74.8%. Alongside comprehensive recycling and waste management programs, Japan also demonstrates leadership in energy conservation and green urban planning that further augment its reputation for environmental sustainability. 19. Belgium Composite Ranking: 19 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 10.8 Waste Management Score: 68%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 68.2% Belgium exemplifies exceptional environmental health, as demonstrated by the EPI Report 2022, which reviews 180 nations based on 40 performance indicators. Belgium's ranking evidences its commitment to mitigating pollution and managing solid waste. 18. Czech Republic Composite Ranking: 18 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 13.4 Waste Management Score: 74.9%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 61.5% The Czech Republic is also recognized as one of the world's cleanest countries, as confirmed by the Environmental Performance Index (EPI) Report 2022. The EPI Report ranked France amongst the top-performing nations because of its air quality, waste management, and climate change adaptation. 17. France Composite Ranking: 17 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 11.5  Waste Management Score: 63.8%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 88% France is one of the cleanest countries in the world largely due to its exceptional wastewater treatment, which is scored 88% as of current. Moreover, the country's solid waste management system scores 63.8% and shows the French government's concerted efforts to prioritize recycling and minimize landfill usage.16. Slovenia Composite Ranking: 16 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 15.1  Waste Management Score: 66.7%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 92.2% Slovenia has achieved a commendable wastewater treatment score of 92.2%, indicating highly efficient removal and neutralization of pollutants from water. Also, the nation's solid waste management rating of 66.7% demonstrates its smart waste reduction, segregation, and recycling which contribute to its low environmental impact and outstanding cleanliness.15. column4: 3 Boring Stocks to Buy as Labor Market Faces a Pivot
column10: [Although the headline print of the June jobs report was encouraging in that it came in below economists’ forecast, it might not be enough for the Federal Reserve, meaning that investors should still consider boring stocks to buy based on the possible labor market impact. Basically, the central bank may start to get serious about inflation.While the disinflationary trend is positive, there’s some work to be done. First, the unemployment rate declined slightly. column4: 25 Cleanest Countries In the World In 2023
column10: [This article will look at the 25 cleanest countries in the world that are performing well on multiple environmental indicators like climate change mitigation, waste management, and air quality. We'll also discuss the continuously deteriorating air and environmental quality. If you want to skip the details, read 10 Cleanest Countries In The World In 2023. Grading the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023 is a subjective topic that requires a deep dive into their environment-related efforts. For instance, the Environmental Performance Index (EPI) offers a broad measure of environmental health and ecosystem vitality, ranking countries based on factors such as air and water quality, biodiversity, and climate and energy policies. The EPI, as of 2022, identified Denmark, Luxembourg, and Switzerland as the leading cleanest countries in the world.But these rankings might vary if we look at more specific indicators. For example, according to IQAir World Report 2022, Iceland has the highest air quality score, closely followed by Australia and New Zealand. Contrarily, these countries' wastewater treatment efforts are ranked 25th, 10th, and 15th, respectively. Moreover, cultural norms and attitudes towards cleanliness, waste management, and littering impact a country's cleanliness. Therefore, assessing a country's cleanliness is a subjective and complex topic, heavily reliant on the specific dimensions evaluated.Sustainability-Focused Waste Management CompaniesForward-thinking waste management companies like Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM), Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN), and Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) are continuously implementing efforts to make waste dumping sustainable. For instance, Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM) has goals like greenhouse gas emissions reduction and responsible waste dumping. The company has started producing renewable fuels by capturing gases released from its landfills and converting it into low-carbon fuel that supports a portion of its fleet. Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM) has a current market cap of $68.484 billion and it is one of the largest waste management companies in the USA. Story continuesMoreover, Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN), the third-largest solid waste management company in North America, that boasts a current market cap of $36.346 billion, increased the use of robotics in its recycling facility and consistently recycles 50% of its collected waste. Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN) also processes 50% of its leachate on-site and has completed the construction of two new leachate plants in 2022 to meet its groundwater safety goals. Arizona-based Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) is also focused on responsible environmental solutions for the residential sector. For instance, Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) has recorded a 9% reduction in its operational greenhouse gas emissions since 2017 and aims to drop this level to 10% by 2025. The company is also close to opening the country's first fully integrated plastic recycling facility in Las Vegas, named Polymer Center, by the end of this year, that'll aim to produce 100 million pounds of recycled plastic annually. Waste management companies are now focusing on recycling and clean energy sources more than ever. If you wish to be a part of these progressive mitigation efforts, read 11 Best Waste Management Stocks to Buy Now, and add more weight to your investment strategy. Which Is The No 1 Cleanest Country In The World?As per our recent analysis of multifaceted environmental parameters, Luxembourg is the cleanest country in the world in 2023. The country has exhibited an exemplary approach towards waste management, boasting an impressive recycling rate. Coupled with legislation and progressive public attitudes, this has facilitated a highly effective waste disposal system and minimized the country's environmental contamination. The wastewater treatment facilities in Luxembourg also display advanced technical acuity, achieving near-perfect filtration rates and significantly reducing aquatic pollution. This treatment proficiency and a remarkable level of infrastructure investment contribute to the nation's place among the top 10 cleanest countries in the world in 2023.Which Is The Cleanest Country In Asia?Japan's concerted efforts towards ecological sustainability confidently assert the country's distinction of being the cleanest country in Asia. Japan's initiatives focused on environmental preservation, particularly its commitment to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and developing renewable energy resources, have proven instrumental in setting new benchmarks for sustainable living. The country's environmentally-friendly policies are backed by robust infrastructure encouraging green practices and waste management.We have already covered 30 Least Polluted Countries in the World; give this detailed article a read to learn the planet's pollution dynamics. Which Is The Least Clean Country In The World?The Environmental Performance Index (EPI) 2022 report ranks India as the dirtiest country in the world, primarily due to its high population density, considerable vehicular congestion, and extensive biomass fuel usage. India's population growth, which is currently surpassing China, poses environmental challenges and calls for expansive mitigation efforts. For instance, urbanization and vehicular traffic explosion have badly impacted the country's air quality and propelled it to the bottom of the list. High emission levels from vehicles, combined with inadequate waste management, contribute to an alarming increase in air, water, and soil pollution. Additionally, India's reliance on biomass fuels, primarily in rural areas, further compounds the pollution problem. These fuels, including firewood, cow dung, and crop residues, emit substantial amounts of pollutants when burned. While India has tried to mitigate these issues, the magnitude of the challenges requires extensive environmental-friendly policies, justifying its ranking as the least clean country in the world per the EPI Report 2022.25 Cleanest Countries in the World in 202325 Cleanest Countries in the World in 2023Our Methodology To rank the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023, we relied on their air quality index, waste management system, and availability of wastewater treatment networks. To understand these crucial parameters, we referred to the Environmental Performance Index Report 2022 (collectively published by Yale and Columbia University), which analyzes 180 countries according to 40 environmental performance indicators. Our first step was to shortlist 25 countries with the best overall EPI score in 2022 (given that it is awarded based on extensive variables, these countries are doing well overall). Then, as solid waste management and wastewater treatment determine a country’s determination towards being ‘clean,’ we picked these two variables from the EPI Report and shortlisted 25 countries with the highest score in these categories. The report has awarded wastewater treatment scores to countries depending on what percentage of a nation’s wastewater undergoes at least some kind of treatment. For example, if a country’s whole population is connected to a sewerage system and all of the collected wastewater is treated, its score will be 100%. Similarly, the EPI Index measures a country’s waste management system according to its efforts to limit solid waste, recycling rates, and oceanic plastic pollution. So if a nation’s solid waste management score is 79%, it indicates its overall performance in these criteria collectively. For our 3rd key metric, i.e., air quality index, we referred to the IQAir World Air Quality Report 2022, which scores countries based on PM2.5 ranking. PM2.5 refers to atmospheric particulate matter (PM) with a diameter of less than 2.5 micrometers. So if a place’s air has particulate matter between 0-12 μg/m³ (micrograms per cubic meter), it is considered good. Likewise, AQI of 12.1-34.5 μg/m³ is moderate, while a μg/m³ score of 55.5-150.4 is unhealthy. In short, the lower the 2.5PM rating, the better a country’s air quality will be.After listing these three variables individually for the top 25 countries, we averaged their scores to get composite rankings to present a broader perspective of their cleanliness levels. Based on our findings, here are the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023: 25. Cyprus Composite Ranking: 25 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 15.6 Waste Management Score: 58.9%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 50%  Our list of cleanest countries in the world in 2023 starts with Cyprus, owing to its moderate wastewater treatment system and solid waste management efforts. Although the country's air quality index is 15.6 (PM2.5 μg/m³ being the best score), its moderate waste system is commendable. Also, stringent regulations on emissions combined with a transition towards renewable energy have significantly improved the country's air quality.24. Croatia Composite Ranking: 24 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 23.5  Waste Management Score: 55.3%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 69% When tested on indicators like environmental performance and eco-friendly waste mitigation, Croatia finds a place amongst the cleanest countries in 2023. The country's stellar environmental status is a result of rigorous national policies that promote renewable energy, waste management, and biodiversity conservation. UNESCO's sustainability index also applauds Croatia's dedication to maintaining pristine ecosystems.23. Italy Composite Ranking: 23 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 18.9  Waste Management Score: 60.6%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 58.8%Italy is also one of the world's cleanest countries in 2023, according to the Environmental Performance Index (EPI). This success can be attributed to the country's rigorous policies on waste management, its substantial investment in renewable energy, and the adoption of eco-friendly practices by the population.22. Slovakia Composite Ranking: 22 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 14.5 Waste Management Score: 62.2%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 44.7%With an impressive waste management score of 62.2%, Slovakia has cemented its place on the list of cleanest places to live in 2023. Data from the Environmental Performance Index shows the country's solid environmental policies, along with a focus on reducing air and water pollution.21. Malta Composite Ranking: 21 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 11.7  Waste Management Score: 63.5%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 14.9% Although Malta's wastewater treatment system isn't as commendable as others on our list, its solid waste management strategies and air quality index make it one of the cleanest places to live in 2023. With an aim to become the leader in green energy deployment, Malta's transition to renewable resources has notably reduced pollution. 20. Japan Composite Ranking: 20 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 9.1  Waste Management Score: 52.8%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 74.8% Japan is the cleanest country in Asia because of the country's culture and modern infrastructure. In 2023, Japan firmly established itself amongst the world's cleanest nations, boasting a wastewater treatment index of 74.8%. Alongside comprehensive recycling and waste management programs, Japan also demonstrates leadership in energy conservation and green urban planning that further augment its reputation for environmental sustainability. 19. Belgium Composite Ranking: 19 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 10.8 Waste Management Score: 68%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 68.2% Belgium exemplifies exceptional environmental health, as demonstrated by the EPI Report 2022, which reviews 180 nations based on 40 performance indicators. Belgium's ranking evidences its commitment to mitigating pollution and managing solid waste. 18. Czech Republic Composite Ranking: 18 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 13.4 Waste Management Score: 74.9%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 61.5% The Czech Republic is also recognized as one of the world's cleanest countries, as confirmed by the Environmental Performance Index (EPI) Report 2022. The EPI Report ranked France amongst the top-performing nations because of its air quality, waste management, and climate change adaptation. 17. France Composite Ranking: 17 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 11.5  Waste Management Score: 63.8%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 88% France is one of the cleanest countries in the world largely due to its exceptional wastewater treatment, which is scored 88% as of current. Moreover, the country's solid waste management system scores 63.8% and shows the French government's concerted efforts to prioritize recycling and minimize landfill usage.16. Slovenia Composite Ranking: 16 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 15.1  Waste Management Score: 66.7%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 92.2% Slovenia has achieved a commendable wastewater treatment score of 92.2%, indicating highly efficient removal and neutralization of pollutants from water. Also, the nation's solid waste management rating of 66.7% demonstrates its smart waste reduction, segregation, and recycling which contribute to its low environmental impact and outstanding cleanliness.15. Latvia Composite Ranking: 15 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 10.1  Waste Management Score: 63%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 90.7% As of 2023, Latvia has one of the best national-level performances in wastewater treatment, marked by a score of 90.7%, which shows its repurposing of water resources and controlling pollution. Coupled with a solid waste management rating of 63%, Latvia has a solid reputation for environmental cleanliness.14. New Zealand Composite Ranking: 14 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 4.8  Waste Management Score: 60.9%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 79.9% New Zealand is one of the cleanest places to live in 2023 as it boasts superior air and water quality metrics. With an air quality index of 4.8, the country has consistently met and exceeded international clean air standards. Plus, a wastewater treatment efficacy score of 79.9% underscores NZ's advanced waste management practices. 13. Estonia Composite Ranking: 13 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 4.9  Waste Management Score: 66.7%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 70.40% Estonia consistently ranks among the globe's cleanest nations because of its eco-friendly policies. The nation has an exceptional air quality score of 4.9 (where 2.5 is the highest), indicating negligible levels of particulate pollution. Its highly efficient wastewater management system, which records a 70.40% treatment score, further attests to the country's stringent environmental protection standards. 12. United Kingdom Composite Ranking: 12 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 8.9  Waste Management Score: 62.6%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 99% The United Kingdom is also one of the cleanest countries in the world because of its laudable wastewater management efficacy. According to the recent EPI Report, the UK's wastewater treatment score is 99%. The outstanding score denotes the efficiency of infrastructure and processes that systematically capture, treat, and safely reintroduce wastewater into the environment.11. Concurrently, the country registered a 7.5 PM2.5 air quality concentration (μg/m³), a low and favorable indicator of particulate pollution.Click to continue reading 10 Cleanest Countries In The World In 2023.Suggested Articles:25 Most Environmentally Friendly Companies in the World25 Cleanest Cities in the U.S.25 Most Polluted Countries in the WorldDisclosure: None. 25 Cleanest Countries In The World In 2023 is originally published at Insider Monkey.]

While this widely-known consensus outlook is important in gauging the company's earnings picture, a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price is how the actual results compare to these estimates.The stock might move higher if these key numbers top expectations in the upcoming earnings report, which is expected to be released on July 31. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.Zacks Consensus EstimateThis waste management company is expected to post quarterly earnings of $1.33 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +0.8%.Revenues are expected to be $3.7 billion, up 8.4% from the year-ago quarter.Estimate Revisions TrendThe consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 1% lower over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.Investors should keep in mind that the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts may not always get reflected in the aggregate change.Earnings WhisperEstimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.Story continuesThus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for Republic Services?For Republic Services, the Most Accurate Estimate is higher than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bullish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of +0.34%.On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #3.So, this combination indicates that Republic Services will most likely beat the consensus EPS estimate.Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?Analysts often consider to what extent a company has been able to match consensus estimates in the past while calculating their estimates for its future earnings. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Republic Services would post earnings of $1.13 per share when it actually produced earnings of $1.24, delivering a surprise of +9.73%.Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates four times.Bottom LineAn earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.Republic Services appears a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.An Industry Player's Expected ResultsAmong the stocks in the Zacks Waste Removal Services industry, GFL Environmental Inc. column4: 3 Boring Stocks to Buy as Labor Market Faces a Pivot
column10: [Although the headline print of the June jobs report was encouraging in that it came in below economists’ forecast, it might not be enough for the Federal Reserve, meaning that investors should still consider boring stocks to buy based on the possible labor market impact. Basically, the central bank may start to get serious about inflation.While the disinflationary trend is positive, there’s some work to be done. First, the unemployment rate declined slightly. Second, the average length of the work week increased. Third, wage growth remained stable and relatively robust on a month-to-month basis. At scale, these factors imply that more dollars are chasing after fewer goods, which of course is inflationary. Therefore, it may be time to consider defense stocks amid market stability concerns.Sure, the market may be hot right now. However, the Fed will want to cool it to meaningfully tame inflation. Thus, the below boring stocks may be a better approach to investing in uncertainty.InvestorPlace - Stock Market News, Stock Advice & Trading TipsRepublic Services (RSG)hands at desk near laptop computer, with one hand holding a pile of hundred dollar bills. Bank stocksSource: shutterstock.com/CC7Almost a no-brainer for boring stocks to buy based on the possible upcoming labor market impact, Republic Services (NYSE:RSG) specializes in recycling services and non-hazardous solid waste disposal. What I appreciate about Republic is that it offers a permanently relevant business. No matter what happens in the economy, people will produce trash. With limited land resources, the industry will almost surely rise in demand long term.Fundamentally, Republic also benefits from a massive moat. Just try and get a permit for a landfill and see how quickly you get rejected. It’s just not happening. And in recent years, developing nations that previously stored North American trash is simply saying no mas. Cynically, such a framework will likely only bolster the waste management industry, making RSG one of the top defensive stocks to consider.Story continuesTo be fair, with RSG trading at a forward earnings multiple of nearly 29 times, you’re not going to get a discount. However, Republic benefits from strong revenue growth and consistent profitability. For investing in uncertainty, RSG makes for a great case.Kelly Services (KELYA)Stocks to buy: smartphone with the words "buy" and "sell" displayed on the screen. The user's finger is about to press buy. Stock charts are in the background of the image. Best Speculative StocksSource: Chompoo Suriyo / Shutterstock.comArguably one of the best boring stocks for the upcoming labor market impact, Kelly Services (NASDAQ:KELYA) at first seems irrelevant. As an employment staffing agency, Kelly inherently offers jobseekers utilitarian value. However, in a tight labor market where labor market growth remains robust, job applicants don’t need middlemen entities. Instead, they can directly apply to positions given the plentiful opportunities available.However, if the Fed imposes an aggressively hawkish monetary policy, said action may affect market stability. Perhaps most noticeably, the labor arena may experience a slackening, where job seekers are many but opportunities are few. In such a scenario, desperation will almost surely rise. And desperation cynically helps Kelly Services.Also, it’s worth noting that Kelly doesn’t just specialize in specific fields, such as accounting and finance. Rather, it runs the whole gamut from white-collar specialties to warehousing/factory jobs. Plus, in a slack labor market, beggars can’t be choosers. Therefore, the shifting power pendulum makes KELYA a strong idea for defensive stocks to buy.Dollar Tree (DLTR)a green button on a keyboard has an arrow pointing upward with the word "Buy". representing safe stocks to buySource: AdityaB. Photography/ShutterStock.comIf the central bank takes the gloves off in its fight against inflation, then discount retailer Dollar Tree (NASDAQ:DLTR) will make a compelling case for boring stocks to buy against a possible labor market impact. Should borrowing costs rise, that will likely negatively affect companies’ expansionary efforts. Layoffs would materialize, thus incentivizing DLTR.Now, what makes DLTR stand out regarding investing in uncertainty is an activist investor-supported turnaround effort. According to The Detroit News, the overhaul depends on improving supply chain capabilities, modernizing technology systems, and lifting wages. Plus, Dollar Tree CEO Rick Dreiling mentioned that the physical stores need to be upgraded.“Our decor right now in both banners is right out of 1975,” Dreiling told analysts at an investor day last month. I couldn’t agree more.Priced at a forward multiple of 24.2X, DLTR isn’t cheap, I must say. However, because of its strong revenue growth and consistent profitability, DLTR is a buy. That’s especially the case because mass layoffs will see consumers shop for discounts.On the date of publication, Josh Enomoto did not have (either directly or indirectly) any positions in the securities mentioned in this article. The opinions expressed in this article are those of the writer, subject to the InvestorPlace.com Publishing Guidelines.A former senior business analyst for Sony Electronics, Josh Enomoto has helped broker major contracts with Fortune Global 500 companies. column4: 25 Cleanest Countries In the World In 2023
column10: [This article will look at the 25 cleanest countries in the world that are performing well on multiple environmental indicators like climate change mitigation, waste management, and air quality. We'll also discuss the continuously deteriorating air and environmental quality. If you want to skip the details, read 10 Cleanest Countries In The World In 2023. Grading the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023 is a subjective topic that requires a deep dive into their environment-related efforts. For instance, the Environmental Performance Index (EPI) offers a broad measure of environmental health and ecosystem vitality, ranking countries based on factors such as air and water quality, biodiversity, and climate and energy policies. The EPI, as of 2022, identified Denmark, Luxembourg, and Switzerland as the leading cleanest countries in the world.But these rankings might vary if we look at more specific indicators. For example, according to IQAir World Report 2022, Iceland has the highest air quality score, closely followed by Australia and New Zealand. Contrarily, these countries' wastewater treatment efforts are ranked 25th, 10th, and 15th, respectively. Moreover, cultural norms and attitudes towards cleanliness, waste management, and littering impact a country's cleanliness. Therefore, assessing a country's cleanliness is a subjective and complex topic, heavily reliant on the specific dimensions evaluated.Sustainability-Focused Waste Management CompaniesForward-thinking waste management companies like Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM), Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN), and Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) are continuously implementing efforts to make waste dumping sustainable. For instance, Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM) has goals like greenhouse gas emissions reduction and responsible waste dumping. The company has started producing renewable fuels by capturing gases released from its landfills and converting it into low-carbon fuel that supports a portion of its fleet. Waste Management Inc (NYSE:WM) has a current market cap of $68.484 billion and it is one of the largest waste management companies in the USA. Story continuesMoreover, Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN), the third-largest solid waste management company in North America, that boasts a current market cap of $36.346 billion, increased the use of robotics in its recycling facility and consistently recycles 50% of its collected waste. Waste Connections Inc (NYSE:WCN) also processes 50% of its leachate on-site and has completed the construction of two new leachate plants in 2022 to meet its groundwater safety goals. Arizona-based Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) is also focused on responsible environmental solutions for the residential sector. For instance, Republic Services Inc (NYSE:RSG) has recorded a 9% reduction in its operational greenhouse gas emissions since 2017 and aims to drop this level to 10% by 2025. The company is also close to opening the country's first fully integrated plastic recycling facility in Las Vegas, named Polymer Center, by the end of this year, that'll aim to produce 100 million pounds of recycled plastic annually. Waste management companies are now focusing on recycling and clean energy sources more than ever. If you wish to be a part of these progressive mitigation efforts, read 11 Best Waste Management Stocks to Buy Now, and add more weight to your investment strategy. Which Is The No 1 Cleanest Country In The World?As per our recent analysis of multifaceted environmental parameters, Luxembourg is the cleanest country in the world in 2023. The country has exhibited an exemplary approach towards waste management, boasting an impressive recycling rate. Coupled with legislation and progressive public attitudes, this has facilitated a highly effective waste disposal system and minimized the country's environmental contamination. The wastewater treatment facilities in Luxembourg also display advanced technical acuity, achieving near-perfect filtration rates and significantly reducing aquatic pollution. This treatment proficiency and a remarkable level of infrastructure investment contribute to the nation's place among the top 10 cleanest countries in the world in 2023.Which Is The Cleanest Country In Asia?Japan's concerted efforts towards ecological sustainability confidently assert the country's distinction of being the cleanest country in Asia. Japan's initiatives focused on environmental preservation, particularly its commitment to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and developing renewable energy resources, have proven instrumental in setting new benchmarks for sustainable living. The country's environmentally-friendly policies are backed by robust infrastructure encouraging green practices and waste management.We have already covered 30 Least Polluted Countries in the World; give this detailed article a read to learn the planet's pollution dynamics. Which Is The Least Clean Country In The World?The Environmental Performance Index (EPI) 2022 report ranks India as the dirtiest country in the world, primarily due to its high population density, considerable vehicular congestion, and extensive biomass fuel usage. India's population growth, which is currently surpassing China, poses environmental challenges and calls for expansive mitigation efforts. For instance, urbanization and vehicular traffic explosion have badly impacted the country's air quality and propelled it to the bottom of the list. High emission levels from vehicles, combined with inadequate waste management, contribute to an alarming increase in air, water, and soil pollution. Additionally, India's reliance on biomass fuels, primarily in rural areas, further compounds the pollution problem. These fuels, including firewood, cow dung, and crop residues, emit substantial amounts of pollutants when burned. While India has tried to mitigate these issues, the magnitude of the challenges requires extensive environmental-friendly policies, justifying its ranking as the least clean country in the world per the EPI Report 2022.25 Cleanest Countries in the World in 202325 Cleanest Countries in the World in 2023Our Methodology To rank the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023, we relied on their air quality index, waste management system, and availability of wastewater treatment networks. To understand these crucial parameters, we referred to the Environmental Performance Index Report 2022 (collectively published by Yale and Columbia University), which analyzes 180 countries according to 40 environmental performance indicators. Our first step was to shortlist 25 countries with the best overall EPI score in 2022 (given that it is awarded based on extensive variables, these countries are doing well overall). Then, as solid waste management and wastewater treatment determine a country’s determination towards being ‘clean,’ we picked these two variables from the EPI Report and shortlisted 25 countries with the highest score in these categories. The report has awarded wastewater treatment scores to countries depending on what percentage of a nation’s wastewater undergoes at least some kind of treatment. For example, if a country’s whole population is connected to a sewerage system and all of the collected wastewater is treated, its score will be 100%. Similarly, the EPI Index measures a country’s waste management system according to its efforts to limit solid waste, recycling rates, and oceanic plastic pollution. So if a nation’s solid waste management score is 79%, it indicates its overall performance in these criteria collectively. For our 3rd key metric, i.e., air quality index, we referred to the IQAir World Air Quality Report 2022, which scores countries based on PM2.5 ranking. PM2.5 refers to atmospheric particulate matter (PM) with a diameter of less than 2.5 micrometers. So if a place’s air has particulate matter between 0-12 μg/m³ (micrograms per cubic meter), it is considered good. Likewise, AQI of 12.1-34.5 μg/m³ is moderate, while a μg/m³ score of 55.5-150.4 is unhealthy. In short, the lower the 2.5PM rating, the better a country’s air quality will be.After listing these three variables individually for the top 25 countries, we averaged their scores to get composite rankings to present a broader perspective of their cleanliness levels. Based on our findings, here are the 25 cleanest countries in the world in 2023: 25. Cyprus Composite Ranking: 25 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 15.6 Waste Management Score: 58.9%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 50%  Our list of cleanest countries in the world in 2023 starts with Cyprus, owing to its moderate wastewater treatment system and solid waste management efforts. Although the country's air quality index is 15.6 (PM2.5 μg/m³ being the best score), its moderate waste system is commendable. Also, stringent regulations on emissions combined with a transition towards renewable energy have significantly improved the country's air quality.24. Croatia Composite Ranking: 24 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 23.5  Waste Management Score: 55.3%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 69% When tested on indicators like environmental performance and eco-friendly waste mitigation, Croatia finds a place amongst the cleanest countries in 2023. The country's stellar environmental status is a result of rigorous national policies that promote renewable energy, waste management, and biodiversity conservation. UNESCO's sustainability index also applauds Croatia's dedication to maintaining pristine ecosystems.23. Italy Composite Ranking: 23 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 18.9  Waste Management Score: 60.6%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 58.8%Italy is also one of the world's cleanest countries in 2023, according to the Environmental Performance Index (EPI). This success can be attributed to the country's rigorous policies on waste management, its substantial investment in renewable energy, and the adoption of eco-friendly practices by the population.22. Slovakia Composite Ranking: 22 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 14.5 Waste Management Score: 62.2%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 44.7%With an impressive waste management score of 62.2%, Slovakia has cemented its place on the list of cleanest places to live in 2023. Data from the Environmental Performance Index shows the country's solid environmental policies, along with a focus on reducing air and water pollution.21. Malta Composite Ranking: 21 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 11.7  Waste Management Score: 63.5%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 14.9% Although Malta's wastewater treatment system isn't as commendable as others on our list, its solid waste management strategies and air quality index make it one of the cleanest places to live in 2023. With an aim to become the leader in green energy deployment, Malta's transition to renewable resources has notably reduced pollution. 20. Japan Composite Ranking: 20 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 9.1  Waste Management Score: 52.8%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 74.8% Japan is the cleanest country in Asia because of the country's culture and modern infrastructure. In 2023, Japan firmly established itself amongst the world's cleanest nations, boasting a wastewater treatment index of 74.8%. Alongside comprehensive recycling and waste management programs, Japan also demonstrates leadership in energy conservation and green urban planning that further augment its reputation for environmental sustainability. 19. Belgium Composite Ranking: 19 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 10.8 Waste Management Score: 68%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 68.2% Belgium exemplifies exceptional environmental health, as demonstrated by the EPI Report 2022, which reviews 180 nations based on 40 performance indicators. Belgium's ranking evidences its commitment to mitigating pollution and managing solid waste. 18. Czech Republic Composite Ranking: 18 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 13.4 Waste Management Score: 74.9%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 61.5% The Czech Republic is also recognized as one of the world's cleanest countries, as confirmed by the Environmental Performance Index (EPI) Report 2022. The EPI Report ranked France amongst the top-performing nations because of its air quality, waste management, and climate change adaptation. 17. France Composite Ranking: 17 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 11.5  Waste Management Score: 63.8%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 88% France is one of the cleanest countries in the world largely due to its exceptional wastewater treatment, which is scored 88% as of current. Moreover, the country's solid waste management system scores 63.8% and shows the French government's concerted efforts to prioritize recycling and minimize landfill usage.16. Slovenia Composite Ranking: 16 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 15.1  Waste Management Score: 66.7%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 92.2% Slovenia has achieved a commendable wastewater treatment score of 92.2%, indicating highly efficient removal and neutralization of pollutants from water. Also, the nation's solid waste management rating of 66.7% demonstrates its smart waste reduction, segregation, and recycling which contribute to its low environmental impact and outstanding cleanliness.15. Latvia Composite Ranking: 15 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 10.1  Waste Management Score: 63%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 90.7% As of 2023, Latvia has one of the best national-level performances in wastewater treatment, marked by a score of 90.7%, which shows its repurposing of water resources and controlling pollution. Coupled with a solid waste management rating of 63%, Latvia has a solid reputation for environmental cleanliness.14. New Zealand Composite Ranking: 14 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 4.8  Waste Management Score: 60.9%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 79.9% New Zealand is one of the cleanest places to live in 2023 as it boasts superior air and water quality metrics. With an air quality index of 4.8, the country has consistently met and exceeded international clean air standards. Plus, a wastewater treatment efficacy score of 79.9% underscores NZ's advanced waste management practices. 13. Estonia Composite Ranking: 13 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 4.9  Waste Management Score: 66.7%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 70.40% Estonia consistently ranks among the globe's cleanest nations because of its eco-friendly policies. The nation has an exceptional air quality score of 4.9 (where 2.5 is the highest), indicating negligible levels of particulate pollution. Its highly efficient wastewater management system, which records a 70.40% treatment score, further attests to the country's stringent environmental protection standards. 12. United Kingdom Composite Ranking: 12 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 8.9  Waste Management Score: 62.6%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 99% The United Kingdom is also one of the cleanest countries in the world because of its laudable wastewater management efficacy. According to the recent EPI Report, the UK's wastewater treatment score is 99%. The outstanding score denotes the efficiency of infrastructure and processes that systematically capture, treat, and safely reintroduce wastewater into the environment.11. Ireland Composite Ranking: 11 Air Quality PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³): 7.5  Waste Management Score: 67.9%  Wastewater Treatment Score: 87% Ireland is amongst the nations with the lowest pollution levels in 2023 because of the government's interest in sustainable waste management. For instance, Ireland achieved an admirable 87% wastewater treatment score in 2022, which reflects the effectiveness of its water purification infrastructure. Concurrently, the country registered a 7.5 PM2.5 air quality concentration (μg/m³), a low and favorable indicator of particulate pollution.Click to continue reading 10 Cleanest Countries In The World In 2023.Suggested Articles:25 Most Environmentally Friendly Companies in the World25 Cleanest Cities in the U.S.25 Most Polluted Countries in the WorldDisclosure: None. 25 Cleanest Countries In The World In 2023 is originally published at Insider Monkey.]

Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.Story continuesThus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate.
